articles.title: Super League: York Knights finish maiden season with thrashing of Bradford Bulls as Paul Vaughan retires
articles.summary: York saw off bottom club Bradford 35-16 in their final match of the regular Super League campaign at the LNER Community Stadium, where Paul Vaughan slotted over a late drop goal on his farewell appearance before retirement.
articles.body:
York Knights finish maiden Super League campaign with home win over bottom side Bradford Bulls; Wigan need to win in Round 27 to clinch League Leaders' Shield; Warrington and Wakefield still in contention for third; regular Super League season concludes live on Sky Sports

York saw off bottom club Bradford 35-16 in their final match of the regular Super League campaign at the LNER Community Stadium, where Paul Vaughan slotted over a late drop goal on his farewell appearance before retirement.

The Knights - looking to solidify a 10th-place finish in their debut Super League season - had Scott Galeano sent to the sin bin after just 13 minutes following a tip tackle on Phoenix Steinwede, with Bulls then having a try for full-back Caleb Aekins ruled out for a forward offload.

Ryan Sutton made the breakthrough to score the opening try for Bradford after 17 minutes, with Chris Atkin slotting over the extras. The lead, though, was short-lived as Galeano marked his return to the action by showing quick feet to then dive over.

Ben Jones-Bishop, who was given a guard of honour ahead of making his 400th career appearance, added another try for the home side, with Cody Hunter converting for a 12-6 lead.

Bradford rallied again as Riley Dean latched on to a spilled kick to touchdown, but York responded again just before half-time as Toa Mata'afa burst down the middle to send the Knights into the break 18-12 ahead.

Bulls prop Ebon Scurr saw his try early in the second half ruled out for an obstruction, before York got themselves over the line again on 51 minutes when Jesse Dee touched down a deft low kick from Paul McShane.

York were in again when Bradford spilled another high ball and Xavier Va'a slid over before David Nofoaluma also capitalised on poor handling to dot down in the 67th minute.

Jayden Okunbor went over to give Bradford a late consolation try with five minutes left before Australian prop Vaughan, 35, slotted over a drop goal - sparking wild celebrations from his York team-mates.

articles.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury: Netflix on board as UK venue emerges
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury appeared to be slipping away, with the long-rumoured venue, Madison Square Garden, being the cause. Team Joshua have made it cle...
articles.body:
Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury appeared to be slipping away, with the long-rumoured venue, Madison Square Garden, being the cause. Team Joshua have made it clear they want the fight in the UK, with Eddie Hearn leading the charge. However, it now appears there is a "strong chance" the fight lands in the UK, with Dan Rafael reporting the Principality Stadium in Cardiff as the likely venue.

Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury: The saga continues

2026 has been littered with updates regarding the negotiations for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury. First, AJ wanted a warm-up fight, with Fury taking two fights to blow away his rustiness. Both came through, with Joshua surviving a nightmare first round against Kristian Prenga.

It appeared that if the fight does indeed happen, it would be destined for MSG, something that has confused fight fans. Hearn has spoken about the deal on a multitude of occasions, making it clear Joshua had signed for the fight to take place at Wembley Stadium.

A new venue has now jumped to the front of the queue.

Dan Rafael reveals the latest on Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury

On his personal X account, Rafael wrote:

"Per sources involved, there is a strong chance #JoshuaFury will indeed take place in the UK at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, on Nov. 28. Capacity 80k+ & has retractable roof. Asked if Netflix was now OK with the move one source said, "I think they're OK." Whatever happens was told it would be resolved next couple of days."

Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury: The Big Fight Weekend verdict

This latest update really feels like a major barrier has been broken through in negotiations. Whether you're Team Fury or Team Joshua, the update from Dan Rafael feels significant.

November 28, in front of a passionate boxing crowd of 80,000, is what this fight deserves. Yes, it's not Wembley, but the Principality has previously hosted two Joshua fights: his wins over Carlos Takam and Joseph Parker. If Wembley is off the table, Big Fight Weekend is backing Cardiff!

articles.title: New Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla has perfect response to the 13-10 win
articles.summary: The Khosla family is going to have to get familiar with their cardiologists if they're going to own the Seahawks!
articles.body:
Death, taxes, and the Seattle Seahawks raising the collective heart rate of the Pacific Northwest. Once again, the Seahawks thrilled the 12th Man with an exhausting, yet exciting game under the lights of prime time. Seattle has seemingly never played a normal game, and that trend continued on Wednesday night as the Seahawks survived an upset bid with backup quarterback Drew Lock filling in for the injured Sam Darnold .

Seattle ultimately won thanks to a clutch interception in the end zone from corner Josh Jobe . Pressured by DeMarcus Lawrence , Patriots quarterback Drake Maye made an all-time boneheaded decision and lobbed a turkey sandwich into the end zone, where it was picked off by Jobe. The Seahawks, facing the seeming inevitability of a tie to force overtime, managed to secure the hard-earned defensive victory to start the year 1-0.

For the 12's, this was simply par for the course. Bizarre, stressful games are what we've come to expect from this team. It's in their DNA. But for the team's new owners, this was a perfect first taste of what it's like to watch Seahawks football. Vinod Khosla took to Twitter to share his excitement from the first victory in his family's ownership era, and describing the win as a "roller coaster" sums it up perfectly.

Vinod Khosla, his wife Neeru and son Neal are going to have to get familiar with their cardiologists, because this is simply how Seahawks games go!

After the game, head coach Mike Macdonald presented the Khosla family with the game ball. Quite the start to their tenure as owners of the franchise.

articles.title: Raiders claim G Bryce Cabeldue off of waivers
articles.summary: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is bringing one of his players from Seattle to Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is bringing one of his players from Seattle to Las Vegas .

Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that the Raiders have claimed guard Bryce Cabeldue off of waivers from the Seahawks . There's no word of a corresponding move to make room for him on the roster.

Kubiak was the Seahawks' offensive coordinator when they drafted Cabeldue in the sixth round last year. He played in eight regular season games for the Super Bowl champs last year, but was waived ahead of Wednesday night's win over the Patriots .

Spencer Burford and Jackson Powers-Johnson are set to be the starting guards for the Raiders when they open their 2026 season against the Dolphins this weekend.

articles.title: F1 Drivers See Madring as a Punishing Street Circuit: Here’s What They Say
articles.summary: F1 drivers check out the new Madring circuit ahead of the Spanish GP, as they discuss the dangers, difficulties in overtaking and getting a lap done, and tal...
articles.body:
F1 drivers check out the new Madring circuit ahead of the Spanish GP , as they discuss the dangers, difficulties in overtaking and getting a lap done, and talk about the La Monumental corner.

Jeddah? Macau? Monaco? Baku? Zandvoort? The new Madring circuit has been compared to a lot of other tracks on the F1 calendar due to its nature and layout. The drivers are bracing for a hard and tough outing in this weekend's Spanish GP. The narrow and high-speed combination never works well for everyone, with the Saudi Arabian GP a prime example in recent times.

Of course, the F1 drivers eventually find a way through to get things right. But still, ahead of the start, they have mixed emotions, with most agreeing that it will be dangerous. Even though some feel it will not be as dangerous as Jeddah already is, the majority agree that defending will be much easier and overtaking much harder, as seen in Monaco.

Even getting a lap right in qualifying will be a challenge, which the F1 drivers accept. Almost everyone has had a run in the simulator, but they are waiting for the real feel, as the speed and power can only be ascertained once someone is really on track. One of its major attractions is the long, banked La Monumental, which, of course, everyone is looking to try in the real car.

Here's a list of F1 drivers speaking about the dangers:

"I have tried in simulator. Scary, I'll say. It's a bit like reminds me a bit of Jeddah. But proper track, really happy to be here and I think the atmosphere here is going to be is going to be one of the best. I think [it can be] very [punishing track]. It all depends what sort of grip level we get. But I think, yeah, there is no room for error. I think I like those those places, like you get punished and is very rare depending on which corner you do a mistake you might get away with it. But in most places there is no margin for it. Hard to say because the sim obviously I cannot try much of the energy stuff. I think overtaking will be hard. It's going to be in my mind closer to Singapore. I don't think there is a place more dangerous than than Jeddah, I think Jeddah is really quite dangerous and I don't think Madrid itself will be will be something like out of of the of the level. I think nobody knows. We have to wait and see."

"Based on the simulator running, I would say so. I think it's going to be one of those races where we're very much focused on qualifying similar to Budapest, Monaco, Zandvoort. It it seems to be a track where it's going to be a big challenge to overtake. It's a shame in a way because I think the the layout is okay, but but there are some features of the circuit which naturally deter overtaking. One of them is the braking for Turn 5, which is curved and that's the real overtaking opportunity and that kind of curved braking takes away any possibility of different lines and and sending one up the inside. So yeah, that's a shame and maybe a bit of an oversight, but it means that we're going to be fully focused on qualifying and to do a good qualifying, of course you need full confidence and that starts from your first lap on on Friday.

"It [La Monumental] could could be interesting, but it's just coming straight after a very high speed chicane, so I think it's going to be a challenge to be close in the first place. But I think as a spectacle it's going to be really cool. I am quite excited to drive that corner. It's the first real banked corner for us. I mean of course we have the last corner in Zandvoort, which is always flat generally in the dry. Turn 3 is more of a low speed with that banking, but this one is more oval-esque except we're turning right. So yeah, if you're turning right on an oval generally that's not good, but yeah, I am excited to drive it. I think it's a cool unique feature and I have heard it looks really nice with the stands all around it. It makes an interesting atmosphere."

"I think Monaco is up more unforgiving. But yeah, I mean, it's not a very forgiving track, no. I think all three circuits now has not much margin, but yeah, it's pretty, yeah, this one definitely doesn't have much scope for error. No, just the track itself. I think it's just it's going to be hard enough for us as drivers. It's very new. For the team, it's going to be new setting up the car. For the engine guys, normally for them, yes, it's a very new PU, but they can sort of look at the previous years to get an idea, whereas here, it's just new for everyone. It's going to be a big challenge and it's not just like a normal basic easy circuit, it's there's a lot going on. It's complicated.

"For me, I've said before that I think the closest thing to it is maybe Macau, like a Macau slash Jeddah kind of thing. So yeah, I think just for all of us getting up to speed and just getting the most out of the package as a as a group will be difficult. Yeah, I don't I think it's [La Monumental] going to be hard to be flat, so it will be a corner. It's not going to be like the last corner in Zandvoort, which you know, you don't it's not a corner. I don't think there's going to be too many lines, but let's see. Maybe they should have invited some of the NASCAR guys to see where they go. How much grip so it seems especially when it comes to a street track, they're more inaccurate. They're less accurate on a street circuit than a normal circuit, for sure. But they're still pretty good."

"It's an interesting track. I mean without saying the obvious, a lot of walls, a lot of high speed corners, a lot of blind corners. Gives me vibes of Macau but more for an F1 track. Little bit concerning the blind spots in some of the corners. Like if there is a car that's stopped on the other side of the corner, I hope they're just quick on the VSCs and the red flags. Inevitably there are going to be a few crashes this weekend. Wish they did something a bit different with the braking zones and not having them too much angled if you know what I mean. Yeah, you got a lot of combined corners which just thinking of overtaking on Sunday it's quite feels like it's quite easy to defend. You just put the car in the middle of the track and and get a car that's going to go past you. So that just means that it will be a more of a deployment overtake than a than a braking overtake. But yeah, it will be challenging.

"I think more technically speaking, there's a lot of corners on this track that will be between 90 and 100% throttle. So, it's like, I think the top teams will be flat out. For the for the midfield teams and the backfield teams are a bigger lift which has a big effect in deployment. So without going too technical, if you can do a corner flat or not massively changes the way the deployment works. And you don't want to go in qualifying suddenly all these corners start to become flat and your deployment starts to move around a lot. That's what we've found in the sim so far. But then just the general thing of it actually quite smooth from what I've seen so far. I think they've ground the braking zone of Turn 5 which was a big concern for us going into the weekend watching the F3 drivers a few weeks ago go around. And then the technical part will be can you make a car that is good over the kerbs from Turn 1 to Turn 5.

"But you want the stiffness in the car for sector two and sector three because actually the stiffer car gives you more load. But then you are going to sacrifice your Turn 1, Turn 2 kerb riding. And then the final thing is, it is one of those weekends where Q3 run two for those guys, Q1 run three for us, you end up just sending it across the kerbs and it's, I mean that Turn 5-6 feels a little bit like I hope there's a rhythm to it and it's actually not that bad but I think there's an angle there that you're going to you're going to just send it. If you get through the other side you're going to be two or three tenths quicker. If you're not and if you don't want to take that risk you lose out on those few tenths. So good. Yeah, I think the other thing which we've seen in the simulator already is the tyres are going to be absolutely screaming. So sector two and sector three is going to be a challenge.

"Not a concern [about safety]. I'm just I'm always a little bit surprised that these tracks are safe. Like even if you talk Miami, like the back straight, the way that it's kinked and you don't have a clear view of what's actually happening in front of you. It's been a discussion point before. I think that I've looked at the barriers. The barriers look like they're all in the good places. The safety barriers have done a good job on those places. Generally, all the hard concrete walls are are okay. Like they're they're not -touch wood – touching for for the most part. But yeah. I think the more the more.

"I worry about the marbles in the race. You could imagine if from what I've heard it's very low grip at this this point in in the weekend they resurfaced the track quite late. I think it was May which if you think about what's the last resurfaced track we did? You know when the oils are still coming off the track. I can't remember Turkey is like the most recent standout one that that we had. You then form a single line because all the rubber is only in one place and if you could stay away from that line then there's no grip. So on top of trying to find clean air and trying to go up high on the banking, you'll have marbles to contend with as well later in into the race. So you got to be careful with that. Personally, I don't think you can do that many lines. The track's quite narrow and it's different when you have clean air and and there's space, whereas if you have a little snap you're into the wall immediately. Drivers aren't as willing to stick it up to the top of the banking and take the risk of running a high line. So not sure. I hope I'm proving wrong, but I think that part of the track's not going to offer that much overtaking."

"I mean, obviously I did a few laps, some laps on the road behind the road car and two laps I think in a Formula 1 car, but with cameras all around and with a lot of dust on track, but it looked like a very challenging track and I think exactly the kind of tracks that I enjoy as a driver. It's true to say as well that I think coming Sunday the amount of overtaking opportunities will be very little, but I think in qualifying it will be a very cool and challenging track for drivers and for that I'm looking forward to it."

"I've actually been around it earlier earlier today, so yeah, it's going to be a very interesting track to drive. Very technical, obviously I think just quite challenging for us and through the weekend trying to put laps together. I think it's one of those tracks that you're not going to feel like you've nailed a lap, honestly half the time. It's going to be sort of there's going to be one or two mistakes in a lap probably all the time. Quite difficult. Not like not like Monaco. I think Monaco was one where we could push flat out and actually have no limitations, so I would say it's not like it's not going to be like that, but I think it definitely is somewhere that is, more so than Monza or something like that.

"You can yes probably make a bit of a difference. I just think it's going to be very challenging for us to put a lap together to feel like you've nailed everything. If you do it's probably going to make quite a big difference. But it's pretty sketchy in places to be honest. Like it'd be very easy to get wrong. It's not somewhere I don't feel like a lot of flow. It's very technical and sort of hard to just hard to put together, but it might be exciting to perform on track."

"Very difficult to say just the layout of everything is very different here, more in line with Zandvoort, the fact you got some kind of cambered corners, off-camber. I think you have a good combination of all speed ranges, slow, medium and high. So I don't know. It's very difficult to predict these things and I don't like to waste my energy doing so, but there's certainly less places that visually look or that we know of that are as much of a test for the car compared to Monza and being the slow speed and just the overall efficiency of the car with the straight lines. So I'm hoping, yeah, just a few corners can help shift us back in the direction of being more competitive and gives us a better chance of winning.

"I mean, it's a difficult track. We have a lot of blind corners, a lot of corners, you cannot see around, so it's difficult to predict things. This just makes it always a bigger challenge inside the cockpit of a car. The fact you cannot see more than 50% of a corner at one time, so you have these two a lot of braking zones that are combined with a lot of steering, so I don't know what challenges we'll have, but we have all of them, but yeah, the same for everyone. And I was excited, like I mean I always enjoy coming to a new circuit and trying to go to a new place, it's also you have to see it as an opportunity for yourself to try and prepare in the best way possible and use what you can to your advantage and try and make something useful out of it, so yeah, I look forward to just the fact it's a new track, no one's driven it well for a couple, and we look forward to the challenge."

"Yeah, I mean, I just I said in the TV pen before when I heard about the 20 red flags in F3, I was a bit surprised. And then after I drove on the sim, I was surprised there's only 20 red flags. So it's a crazy circuit. I would put it arguably what the the most risky circuit of the whole calendar because you have real high-speed corners, sort of Jeddah-esque. The walls are very close, so there's no margin for error. But then you have other corners that are quite like Baku where you're coming from a high speed into a slow braking zone. You're braking and turning at the same time, so locking tyres are going to be easy and if you lock up, you'll be straight in the wall. So excited to try that out. I think it's going to be really challenging for us as drivers. The race is going to be challenging to overtake, so on the whole it's it's not an easy one."

"I'll put my money on the red flag, that's for sure. Driving wise, I must say in the sim it was very enjoyable and very exciting. I got a good read and feel of pretty much every single wall at every single corner. So actually I know what to do and what not to do. But I think it's going to be very challenging, especially in terms of evolution. Probably a lot of track evolution kind of slightly off-track braking zones which are not fully straight, kind of like snaky, very twisty type of corners, many corners, a lot of blind banking up and downs, undulation all the way.

"So I think yeah, I expect a very tricky track, challenging for us, which makes it good because you can always aim to a bit more difference driving wise. But again as a type of track a bit like Monaco where I think if you do a slight mistake you can have big consequence straight away. So it's about risk and reward every single braking zone and sort of speed that you carry through the corners and yeah. Must say it's exciting. At the same time I think it's going to be quite disruptive weekends from yeah, how easy it will be to have a crash."

"Well, it could be like yeah, in some places of course when you have a tiny moment it can result in a crash but I mean Jeddah is the same. We've spoken about that already before, so you just have to deal with it. Try to figure out the margins of course, try to keep it under control but of course when you're on the limit it's easy to make a little mistake but let's just see how do we can go."

"I think the track seems difficult, first of all, to learn, very technical, a lot of kerb riding and a couple of high-speed sections where you need to get very close to the walls, which is very attractive and very high adrenaline for a driver. Close to Jeddah, I think, some sections. But then, as I said, I think one thing is the simulator and then reality always gives you a different feeling. So, I'm looking forward to FP1 and learning the track, you know, from the car and discovering all these details, you know, that always change a little bit the perception of what you came with, an idea, from the simulator. I think the grip level will be probably the biggest thing for me. If the track is dusty and too dirty at the beginning, that masks a little bit the learning process and, in a way, the fun of it, because you are just taking a lot of risk and unwanted risk because the car is not really responding to your inputs.

"And then you only get to quali and the race when the track is in a good place. But we have F3, we have F2, so maybe the track can be, you know, already good on Friday. If that's the case, I think we have a very good weekend in front of us as a show, you know, for everyone else. And regarding the quali and the race, I think all the street circuits are rewarding more quali. I struggle to believe that the race on Sunday will be better than the quali on Saturday in terms of, you know, rewarding and driver feeling. This year Sundays sometimes are fun as well to watch because, you know, this battery championship, you just overtake. There are unwanted overtakes, you know. In Monza, even for us, I did two or three overtakes and I didn't want to overtake in that place, but the car in front of me was just, you know, with an empty battery and I overtook. But it was not the plan."

"Yeah, the laps in the road car, to be honest, the track was not completed, so nowhere as representative as the laps that I did in the simulator the other day. I think those were proper laps, and then a few onboard laps that we're watching from the F3 test and some data that we've been on to try and prepare as much as possible. But realistically speaking, it's going to be now tomorrow in FP1 when we really know what this track is all about. And I'm going to say it looks different. It looks that the track has character, that is charismatic, with a lot of different kinds of corners. And at least we can take that away, that that is going to be a different track to what we're used to."

"I think basically all the corners are very challenging, but, you know, probably T5 and T6 are going to be very challenging with, you know, lots of kerb usage there, and then going a bit uphill and then downhill, and then having some high-speed corners just after. I think that's the typical type of track that you finish a lap and you can really feel your breathing, you know, because it's very mentally exhausting through the lap. And to nail a perfect lap is also difficult, but when you do it, it's very, very promising."

articles.title: Washington football feeling optimistic about status of injured RB
articles.summary: The Washington Huskies shared an encouraging update surrounding the status of running back Jordan Washington.
articles.body:
The Washington Huskies saw their top two running backs, second-year Quaid Carr and fourth-year Jayden Limar, both suffer significant injuries in the Apple Cup, dealing a significant blow to Jedd Fisch's backfield

However, during his Thursday press conference, Fisch delivered some good news about the injury-ravaged position, as third-year running back Jordan Washington continues to recover from a neck injury that he suffered during spring practice, stating that there's a chance the former four-star recruit returns this season.

"I am more optimistic (that Washington can play in 2026) based upon how his rehab has gone," Fisch said on Thursday.

"He's gotten a lot stronger; he's stronger than he was before he got hurt, with all of his weight room metrics...His speed is the same; the thing that we have to look at is cleared for contact. That decision gets made by the surgeon who took care of him, and then we have to look at conditioning. But in terms of how things are trending, he's doing exceptionally well, but we don't know anything until he gets scanned, and the scans—we're not ready for that yet."

Fisch added that a potential return could happen before the end of the season, but at the same time, tried to temper expectations around what that may look like, adding that he has several benchmarks to hit before he can even get scanned in an attempt to return.

"We'd have to get him into football shape and football conditioning," Fisch added. "He has to go through training camp in terms of two days of practice with just helmets, three days of practice in shoulder pads, and then full pads, so there's an acclimation. If you don't participate in training camp, you have to go back to the training camp acclimation. I don't know exactly the days, but we're probably talking about once he gets cleared, you're not playing him on that Saturday by any means; it's still going to take some time after that."

"I'm not thinking we're bringing back the workhorse running back...when he can come back, if he passes medically, he would give us another set of legs and another ball carrier for us."

articles.title: Everton Take A Big Decision On January Right-Back Signing: Does It Show A Lack Of Ambition?
articles.summary: Everton have reportedly decided against adding another right-back in January, despite concerns over depth. According to a report by The Athletic published on...
articles.body:
Everton have reportedly decided against adding another right-back in January, despite concerns over depth. According to a report by The Athletic published on September 10, the club believe their current options can cover the role after the late arrival of the £4m summer signing from Lyon, Ainsley Maitland-Niles .

That decision follows a dramatic deadline day. The 29-year-old made an immediate impact against Manchester United , scoring a 96th-minute equaliser in a 2-2 draw. David Moyes now expects him to compete with Merlin Rohl for the starting berth, while James Garner and Jake O'Brien can cover when required. They can help on the left, with Jarrad Branthwaite and Garner able to step across if Vitalii Mykolenko misses out.

The thinking comes after Everton failed to sign Celtic' s Alistair Johnston , their preferred target before injury disrupted the move. The collapse of the Folarin Balogun deal added to a frustrating summer under the Friedkin Group, yet the hierarchy believes a defensive purchase can wait.

Does Everton's right-back plan show a lack of ambition?

I don't agree with Everton's decision. A spectacular debut from a £4m signing makes a wonderful story, but one late equaliser can't become the evidence for a squad strategy. Moyes needs reliable options across the season, where injuries, suspensions and fixture congestion can turn depth into a problem.

PRESTON, ENGLAND – AUGUST 26: David Moyes, manager of Everton waves to Preston fans after the Carabao Cup Second Round match between Preston North End and Everton at Deepdale on August 26, 2026 in Preston, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Rohl deserves support, and his willingness to perform at right-back has helped Everton, but asking a young midfielder to become a dependable specialist over months is risky. The same applies to both players. Each can cover the flank, yet every switch creates another hole elsewhere. Pull Garner wide, and you lose a midfield option; use O'Brien there, and you reduce central defensive depth. That is poor squad economics, before fatigue enters the picture.

Everton's summer business makes the decision harder to defend. Missing Johnston exposed the original weakness, while spending £4m on a versatile player solved part of the issue rather than erasing it. Fans can question the Friedkin Group's appetite for a European push when the club have chosen restraint after a thin window.

Moyes should have a specialist right-back available for competition and insurance, rather than rely on emergency reshuffles. A cautious January policy may protect the balance sheet, but it could damage the season if injuries arrive together. For a club chasing Europe, hoping every makeshift solution holds up is a gamble.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase eyeing Super Bowl, good health to begin Bengals season
articles.summary: There are now many signs pointing to Cincinnati Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase being full-go for the team's season-opener against Tampa Bay.
articles.body:
There are now many signs pointing to Cincinnati Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase being full-go for the team's season-opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . That's a good starting point for the latest Bengals player to indicate his only goals for the 2026 season are to win the Super Bowl.

Speaking during a Sept. 10 news conference at Paycor Stadium, Chase said he felt good and has taken on his normal workload in practice. Chase injured his knee during an Aug. 25 training camp practice when he collided with cornerback DJ Turner II.

The missed practices for Chase that followed the collision were precautionary, he said. Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor said he anticipated both Chase and receiver Tee Higgins would be available for the Sept. 13 home opener, and Chase was listed in the Sept. 9-10 injury reports as a full participant in practice.

With health seemingly no longer threatening his ability to begin the season on time, Chase is set to begin his sixth NFL season with Super Bowl aspirations, but no personal or statistical aims he felt were worth mentioning during his Sept. 10 news conference.

"I don't have any personal goals this year," Chase said, "beside the Super Bowl and the AFC (championship). The other stuff is gonna come with that stuff."

Chase also begins 2026 as a team captain for the second year in a row. That task, Chase said, requires him to lead by example and with his words.

"The thing overall with being a captain is obviously, the whole team is looking at me," Chase said. "Everyone is really looking at me, asking me things and just expecting me to do the right thing. I always lead by example but I think it's just being more vocal."

articles.title: Suzy Kolber opens up about ESPN firing, emotional reaction: 'I lost it'
articles.summary: Suzy Kolber revealed the emotional phone call and non-disparagement clause that followed her ESPN layoff after 27 years hosting "Monday Night Countdown."
articles.body: Suzy Kolber was part of a 20-talent layoff at ESPN in June 2023, along with Steve Young, Max Kellerman and Jalen Rose. At the time, Kolber hosted the network’s "Monday Night Countdown" pregame show. Kolber spoke about her firing for the first time during a conversation on the "Sports Media with Richard Deitsch" podcast this week. "He [ESPN president Jimmy Pitaro] said, ‘Suzy there’s a whiteboard and your name’s on it. I don’t really know for sure right now but your name is on it,'" she said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE It’s unclear how the head of the company didn’t know whether Kolber was safe. Nonetheless, she recalled coming home that night and having a conversation with her daughter. "I remember that day sitting next to my daughter in the kitchen. For years I’ve said ‘You never know.’ And I sat down next to her and I cried. And I said, ‘I think this is really happening.’" The following week, Kolber received a call from then-ESPN executive Norby Williamson, best known as a supporter of Mark Jones. Kolber said she "lost it" when Williamson told her she couldn’t say "anything disparaging about the company or we can take the last year of your contract." Before her layoff, Kolber had agreed to take a pay cut. "I did think the 39% cut was going to get me to the end [of my career]," she said. Perhaps Kolber should have remained silent about her firing. She didn’t help herself with these comments. For one, she comes off as entitled. We understand that a layoff can be emotional, regardless of the circumstances. However, a non-disparagement provision is standard. Kolber is no different from any other talent laid off with time remaining on their contract. There was hardly a reason to "lose it," as she put it, over the clause. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Kolber also worked at ESPN for 27 years. She is now 62. She hosted the network’s top pregame show. ESPN didn’t owe her anything else. And yet, she suggested that she was unhappy with the lack of appreciation she received during her departure. "I just thought after 27 years of, I was the first person hired for the launch of ESPN 2. I was the first person assigned to the X Games," she continued. "I went and shot the marketing tape for it. ‘Monday Night Football’s’ move to ESPN, I was part of some pretty big franchises. You’re not going to say a word? Not thanks for 27 years, just acknowledge it? I didn’t understand that." At least her bosses didn’t fire her on-air, mid-show, as they did Ryan Clark in an apparent attempt to spite OutKick. Our understanding is that Kolber’s firing was about the numbers. The network needed to shed a certain amount of talent salary, and she became expendable because ESPN employed other anchors who could fill her role. ESPN eventually tapped Scott Van Pelt to replace Kolber on "Countdown." ESPN likely would have made a change at the position regardless, with its first-ever Super Bowl broadcast coming this fall. The anchor of "Monday Night Countdown" will also host the Super Bowl and its halftime show. As one of the faces of the network, Van Pelt was a favorite for the position before 2023. The network arguably has more NFL hosts than it has major sports. Van Pelt hosts Mondays. Mike Greenberg hosts the Sunday morning pregame show. Laura Rutledge, the host of "NFL Live," would be the lead football anchor at most networks and arguably should be at ESPN. Therefore, Kolber became the odd person out. Still, Kolber was a good host. Her talent and production were not the issues. In fact, since executive Burke Magnus is in the business of rehiring previous anchors, he should have brought her back. Instead — in what appears to be a make-good for firing Ryan Clark — Magnus rehired Stan Verrett, who has a weird obsession with OutKick and race talk, to anchor a show on NFL Network. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Kolber has since shifted her focus, creating a new interview series called "The Originals" on the Scripps Sports Network. Her first episode airs Sept. 15 at 8 p.m.

articles.title: English Open: Liam Davies beats world champion Wu Yize to set up Mark Williams match
articles.summary: World champion Wu Yize is knocked out of the English Open in the third round as he loses 4-1 to Liam Davies, who faces fellow Welshman Mark Williams next.
articles.body:
World champion Wu Yize fell in the third round of the English Open as Liam Davies scored an eye-catching 4-1 victory in Brentwood.

Welsh prospect Davies, 20, opened up a 3-0 lead on his way to the first ranking event quarter-final of his career, helped by a break of 105 in the second frame, then completed his victory as China's Wu struggled to find his dynamic best form.

Tantalisingly, Davies will face compatriot Mark Williams, the three-time world champion, in the last eight on Friday evening.

Williams, still a major force on the baize at the age of 51, had breaks of 76, 103 and 63 in a late-night 4-1 victory over England's Barry Hawkins.

Mark Selby, who was runner-up at last week's British Open and won the China Open in August, had his hopes of reaching another final ended by a 4-3 defeat against fellow former world champion Kyren Wilson.

Selby led 2-0 in the all-English tussle after an early break of 112 but then lost the next three frames. He dragged himself level, but Wilson trebled in the yellow to effectively make sure of victory in the decider.

England's Judd Trump, newly deposed as world number one, edged a tense decider against Scot Anthony McGill to take a 4-3 victory.

Trump will face a quarter-final against Shaun Murphy who was taken the distance after midnight by Pang Junxu before racing through the deciding frame with a 103 break.

Ali Carter had a highest break of 75 as he completed a 4-2 win over Gong Chenzhi, Zhou Yuelong made a 141 in his 4-2 victory over Chinese compatriot Yuan Sijun, and Ding Junhui beat Joe O'Connor 4-1.

articles.title: Texas A&M's Mike Elko describes fight between LSU, SEC over former NFL players as 'parenting'
articles.summary: Mike Elko compared the SEC's clash with Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers to parenting, saying the school backed down once "dad raised his voice."
articles.body: The SEC, no stranger to attention, is once again the center of the college football world. Though not necessarily due to a dominant dynasty racking up championship after championship. Lane Kiffin, also no stranger to attention, immediately invited controversy after taking over as head coach of the LSU Tigers by working to bring in former college players who have signed contracts to play in the NFL. The SEC and Big Ten immediately moved to ban pro players from playing, leading to a series of court battles to settle the issue. While LSU ultimately prevailed, with a judge granting an injunction to let two players, Dae’quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, play this season, the SEC and other teams signaled their intention to fight back. Hard. LSU LEAVES FORMER PRO-ATHLETES OFF FINAL ROSTER, ONE NIGHT BEFORE SEC TAKES LANE KIFFIN AND TIGERS TO COURT The conference cited Kiffin’s flippant, sarcastic comment before halftime during the game against Clemson in a new amended complaint: "Imagine if we had pro players." It was then widely reported that the conference’s other 15 schools would vote to kick the Tigers out at a meeting scheduled for Sept. 10. A brief war of words ensued, resulting in the Tigers seemingly backing down by adding two non-pro players to the roster and filling out their final two spots. Some commentators, like Stephen A. Smith, have defended LSU’s actions, while many opposing coaches have expressed a mixture of skepticism, bewilderment or anger over how Kiffin and the Tigers’ administration handled the situation. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE One of Kiffin’s rival SEC coaches, Texas A&M’s Mike Elko, just added to it Thursday with a colorful explanation of the dynamic between the two opposing sides. "This is a little bit like the son figuring out where the limits are until dad comes home and raises his voice, and then the son goes, ‘I was just kidding, I didn’t mean any of that,'" Elko said. "I think that’s what you’re seeing. LSU will be in the SEC…This is just a little bit of parenting going on right now." Mike Elko, never one to shy away from a great quote. There’s some truth to that, and it’s evidenced not just by how the administration and Kiffin have handled this situation, but how the governor of Louisiana handled it too. After seemingly backing the Tigers, Gov. Jeff Landry issued a statement to Yahoo Sports! regarding the potential vote which said simply, "Ridiculous. Can we just play football?" THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Well, that’s part of the problem, isn’t it? Kiffin’s search for any advantage, no matter how minute, led the Tigers to push the boundaries of what other teams and, ultimately, fans find acceptable. For weeks, LSU backers proudly insisted they were right about bringing NFL players back to college football. As soon as the stakes were raised — for example, with the possibility of expulsion from the conference — the message became, "Can we just play football?" The turn of phrase Elko used might be colorful, but it’s right. LSU was the upstart teenager, who got his bluff called by dad. Dad won out, and now the tone of the conversation has changed. articles.title: How Aryna Sabalenka’s fiancé Georgios Frangulis built his own empire before becoming her biggest supporter
articles.summary: International Sports News: Long before he was cheering from the players' box at Grand Slams, Georgios Frangulis was building something of his own. The Brazilian entrepreneur dro.
articles.body: Long before he was cheering from the players' box at Grand Slams, Georgios Frangulis was building something of his own. The Brazilian entrepreneur dropped out of law school, founded an açaí brand called Oakberry in 2016, and grew it into a global business with more than 800 stores across 50 countries. Now 37, Frangulis proposed to world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in March 2026, capping a relationship that began when she signed on as an Oakberry brand ambassador in early 2024.Who is Georgios Frangulis, Aryna Sabalenka's fiancé?Born and raised in São Paulo, Brazil, Frangulis has Greek roots, with his family originally from Thessaloniki, Greece. He studied law at FAAP -- Fundação Armando Alvares Penteado -- in 2014, but never sat the bar exam."I always knew I wouldn't be a lawyer," he said. "What I really wanted was to be an entrepreneur."That clarity of purpose was rare at the time. Most people spend years hedging. Frangulis walked away from a law degree, moved to the United States, where he became infatuated with açaí, came back to São Paulo, and launched Oakberry in December 2016.How did Georgios Frangulis build Oakberry into a global brand?Co-founded alongside Renato Haidar, Oakberry was not just another smoothie shop. Frangulis positioned açaí as functional nutrition -- clean ingredients, no artificial syrups, and a strong link to fitness culture -- and built a franchise model designed from day one to scale internationally.The company raised $67 million in capital in late 2023. By mid-2026, Oakberry had grown to a 900-location global business, with stores in Dubai malls, Miami gyms, Australian beach towns, and European city centres -- all without compromising brand consistency.In June 2023, Frangulis graced the cover of Forbes Brazil. The profile explored not just his entrepreneurial arc but his spirituality and Greek identity. His bicep tattoo reads "Fight for us, Saint George the Warrior." His forearm reads, "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." These are not the accessories of a brand persona.His net worth in 2026 is estimated between $75 million and $100 million -- built almost entirely from his equity in Oakberry, not from market listings or quick exits.When did Aryna Sabalenka and Georgios Frangulis start dating?They met in January 2024 when Sabalenka was hired as an ambassador for Oakberry. The couple were first spotted together in April 2024 -- a month after the tragic and untimely death of Sabalenka's ex-boyfriend, Konstantin Koltsov, who died by suicide in March 2024.It was a difficult period, and Sabalenka has been open about what Frangulis meant to her during it. "There was a really tough period where I was really happy to have him by my side, always cheering me up, always making sure that we are doing some fun stuff," she told People. "His support means so much to me. Being on the road and having him support me, to make me laugh and to be able to work out together, makes life on the road feel more like home."How did Georgios Frangulis propose to Aryna Sabalenka?Sabalenka had been broadly hinting for months. After winning the Brisbane International in January 2026, she said in her victory speech: "Thank you to my boyfriend... Hopefully soon I can call you something else, right? Let's just put some extra pressure."Frangulis proposed to Sabalenka in Indian Wells, California, on March 3, 2026. The setting was candlelit, with rose petals arranged beside a pool -- a rental home the couple had spent time in since the early days of their relationship. Sabalenka, in jeans and a white t-shirt, had no idea it was coming."I always knew I wanted to propose to Aryna because I was 100% sure she was the person I wanted to spend the rest of my life with," he shared in a YouTube video about the moment.The ring was designed by Isabela Grutman, who worked with Frangulis for months to create the custom piece. It features a 12-carat, oval-cut diamond surrounded by emeralds set in platinum -- Sabalenka's favorite stone, and also her birthstone. Experts told InStyle the ring could be worth up to $1 million. They captioned their joint Instagram post: "You & me, forever."What is 'The Gride,' Georgios Frangulis's new fashion brand?Earlier in 2026, Frangulis launched his own fashion brand, named The Gride. The name honors his Greek heritage and mixes the words Greek and Pride. "My pride comes from my grandparents and has spread to my closest circle," the brand's website states. "The feeling is unmatched, and I'll do my best to make each and every one of you feel it too."Outside business, Frangulis races Porsche GT3 Cup cars. "Getting in the car and racing is one of the few moments when nothing else matters," he told Forbes Brazil. For someone whose professional life spans dozens of countries and time zones, that says something about how he recharges.What is clear is that Frangulis arrived in this relationship with his own story already written. He built a global company from a fruit most of the world had never heard of, then quietly showed up for the woman he loves at every stop on the tour. That is not a supporting role. It is just a different kind of ambition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: You never rat out the guy who fixes your messes. That is locker room rule No. 1. But podcast queen and former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho apparently missed the memo, trading loyalty for views. Now Philadelphia Eagles Chief Security Officer Dom DiSandro, known as "Big Dom," faces an NFL investigation after Acho publicly recounted the incident. On his "Speakeasy" podcast, Acho (formerly an Eagle) recounted a car wreck from his playing days in Philadelphia. He rear-ended a vehicle on his way to practice, panicked and called team security. I’m going to send you another cop and that other cop is going to say it wasn’t your fault, it was their fault.’ I was like, ‘Wait, they do that?’ So, I hit him," Acho said. "Cop comes up. ‘Hey, everything good?’ I’m like, ‘Everything’s good, don’t worry about it. Somebody is going to come here.’ That cop leaves. We send another cop. The other cop that comes to document says she’s at fault. "And they were like, ‘Oh, no, we’re fine.’" According to Acho, Big Dom helped bury the incident, only for that favor to come back and put him under the NFL’s microscope years later. The NFL previously fined him $100,000 and suspended him from the sidelines following a 2023 dustup with 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw. Acho sold out Big Dom’s loyalty for cheap podcast clout. We have an investigation going on because fool is dying for attention and a gossip queen smfh." articles.title: Texas vs. Ohio State has played out in recruiting for years
articles.summary: Brandon Baker is one of the big head-to-head recruiting wins for the Longhorns over the Buckeyes.
articles.body:
"Every week we play teams with players from from the state of Texas."

Steve Sarkisian's Thursday comment about the inevitability of facing off against players from the Lone Star State competing for other programs is certainly a truism. After all, the state of Texas averages well over 300 players per year signing with FBS programs around the country, consistently the highest number of any state in the country.

Even an FCS powerhouse like the Montana Grizzlies have double-digit Texas players on their roster, some from high school recruiting and a handful more out of the portal.

But when the No. 4 Texas Longhorns face off against the No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday in Austin in one of the most highly-anticipated non-conference matchups of the 2026 season, those players will look almost entirely different — they were elite recruits, not the type of lower-tier or mid-tier prospects who make up the rosters of the Texas State Bobcats and UTSA Roadrunners , the other two non-conference opponents for the Longhorns this year.

"Ohio State's recruiting the really good ones, and so Ryan [Day]'s done a really good job of getting players from the state, and they've gone on to produce and play at a high level," Sarkisian said.

The relevant recent history extends back to the Urban Meyer era, when the former Ohio State head coach took advantage of the struggles in Austin to win the high-profile recruiting battles for Texas prospects like running back JK Dobbins, linebacker Baron Browning , and cornerback Jeffrey Okudah in the 2017 recruiting class.

Since Day took over as the full-time head coach after the 2018 season, the two programs have continued to engage in high-profile recruiting battles as Texas suffered a big loss like missing on Lake Travis wide receiver Garrett Wilson — who at least grew up in the Columbus area — and losses that seemed bigger at the time, like the Buckeyes flipping Missouri wide receiver product Mookie Cooper or landing wide receiver Caleb Burton out of Austin.

One massive missed evaluation still lingers over the shared recruiting history of the two programs, too — former head coach Tom Herman and his staff never even offered wide receiver Jaxson Smith-Njigba out of Rockwall, even though he finished the cycle as a consensus five-star prospect. Once intent on playing at either Oklahoma or Texas , neither school showed enough interest as Ohio State recruited him hard.

Even a high-profile flip from the Buckeyes to the Longhorns failed to pay off much for Texas. Consensus top-100 prospect Terrance Brooks , a cornerback from Little Elm, switched his pledge from Ohio State to Texas on Early Signing Day in 2021. Although Brooks did start 16 games over two seasons in Austin, recording three interceptions in 2023, he transferred to Illinois in 2024 with his starting job in jeopardy, got buried on the depth chart in Champaign, and left the team before the bowl game without returning to the Illini.

Even as Sarkisian resurrected the Texas program after its decade in the college football wilderness, Ohio State has continued to win its share of recruiting battles, especially in the state.

The most high-impact recent win for the Buckeyes came in a recruitment the Longhorns had trouble countering when Galena Park North Shore product Devin Sanchez , the No. 1 cornerback in the 2025 class, decided early on that he wanted to leave the state, negating the impact of a late push from the Horns before the early signing period.

After earning one start last year, Sanchez is on track to become a star for Ohio State as he moves into a full-time starting role.

The linebacker position in Columbus features three head-to-head recruiting wins in 2024 signee Payton Pierce , 2025 signee Riley Pettijohn , and 2026 portal addition Christian Alliegro .

A Lucas Lovejoy product, Pierce was similar to Sanchez in showing little interest in the Longhorns despite receiving an offer from Texas early in the process. Florida State , Oklahoma , Texas A&M, and Tennessee were all able to secure visits from Pierce, who gave a spring commitment to Ohio State shortly after an unofficial visit and took his single official visit to Columbus before signing with the Buckeyes as the nation's No. 15 linebacker.

Pierce's contributions steadily increased from his freshman to his sophomore season when he recorded 43 tackles, an interception, a force fumble, and a fumble recovery while starting three games. This year, he'll start at middle linebacker on Saturday in his return to the Lone Star State.

An elite athlete at the position who ran a 10.77 100-meter dash at McKinney, Pettijohn was a bigger miss for Texas — he was ranked more highly than Pierce as the No. 2 linebacker in the 2025 class and showed more interest in the Longhorns, taking one of his four summer official visits to Austin before committing to the Buckeyes in early July.

After playing sparingly as a true freshman, Pettijohn will factor into the linebacker rotation this season, providing a glimpse of the impact that he can make by leading Ohio State with six tackles in the season opener. The 6'2, 235-pounder could play a diverse role against the Longhorns as a potential spy on Texas quarterback Arch Manning or as a situational edge rusher.

Ohio State also won a head-to-head battle during the portal window last January when Wisconsin transfer Christian Alliegro, the No. 3 transfer linebacker, committed to the Buckeyes over the Longhorns. The starter over Pettijohn at the weak-side position, Alliegro brings veteran leadership and playmaking ability with a tackle for loss in the season opener.

Columbus-area native Rasheem Biles has already softened the blow of missing on Alliegro after forcing two turnovers against Texas State and providing one of the better offseason sound bites from a Texas player during preseason camp when he revealed why he didn't consider Ohio State after leaving Pitt.

"When I made my list and stuff I told my mom, I ain't really trying to be in Columbus," Biles said . "I ain't trying to be a Buckeye. They ain't want me out of high school, and I was right there, so ain't no point in trying to get me now, you feel me?"

The Longhorns have also won a few important high school recruiting battles over the last several cycles, including signing four prospects in the 2024 class who took official visits to Ohio State — offensive lineman Daniel Cruz, offensive lineman Brandon Baker , safety Jordon Johnson-Rubell, and cornerback Kobe Black. Baker and Black will both start for the Horns on Saturday with Baker ranking as one of the team's most important offensive line signees since the program-changing 2022 class.

In the 2025 class, the Buckeyes had Lucas Lovejoy wide receiver Daylan McCutcheon high enough on Brian Hartline's board to host him for an official visit before his recruitment took some turns, including a commitment to the Seminoles before the Longhorns circled back and landed a flip from the nation's No. 13 wide receiver.

Several 2026 recruitments played out between the two schools, too.

Most notably for Texas, the Horns were able to land a summer commitment from Florida running back Derrek Cooper without the benefit of an official visit — Cooper had already taken trips to Alabama , Auburn, Florida State, Georgia, Miami, and Ohio State when he committed to Texas.

When standout Buford edge Dre Quinn decomitted from Clemson last September, Texas seemed like the possible favorite after making a major push for the consensus four-star prospect during the summer, but it was Ohio State that got Quinn on campus in November, landing his pledge and eventual signature.

With Cooper injured and Quinn yet to impact the depth chart, neither is going to make an impact on Saturday, but one potential X-factor for Ohio State is North Forney product Legend Bey, an all-purpose back who had one of the most wild recruitments in the 2026 cycle.

Texas extended an offer in early November when the 5'10, 195-pounder was committed to Tennessee. Three days later, Bey flipped from the Volunteers to the Buckeyes. Then things got crazy — Bey flipped back to UT on Early Signing Day and inked with the Vols. It didn't hold, though, as the new agreements are only binding for the school and not the player, allowing Bey to sign with Ohio State less than three weeks later and enroll in Columbus in January.

In the season opener, Bey flashed his dynamic ability on a 23-yard touchdown catch that started heading towards one sideline and ended on the over side of the field.

The 2027 cycle currently features one big recruiting win for the Buckeyes over the Longhorns with the pledge of California product Marcus Fakatou, a consensus five-star prospect ranked as the No. 2 defensive lineman. Fakatou took official visits to Austin and Columbus in addition to Athens.

And although the game's outcome is unlikely to swing any recruits in attendance, the Longhorns and Buckeyes will continue battling for top prospects in the state and around the nation, and it's possible that a player recruited by both schools makes a game-changing play on Campbell-Williams Field.

articles.title: Final score predictions for Penn State vs. Temple in Week 2
articles.summary: The staff of Nittany Lions Wire is all in on Penn State getting out of Philadelphia with a comfortable victory in Week 2 against Temple.
articles.body:
Penn State is hitting the road for the first time under the leadership of head coach Matt Campbell. After an impressive season debut for the 2026 Nittany Lions , Penn State now heads to Philadelphia to take on the Temple Owls in Lincoln Financial Field, home of Saquon Barkley and the Philadelphia Eagles . Penn State's long history against Temple has been almost as one-sided as they come, but this is the first meeting between the two programs since Penn State's Big Ten championship season of 2016. Despite the time off in the series, Penn State will continue the trend of being a heavy favorite when they line up against Temple this weekend.

Here are our game predictions for this weekend's matchup between Penn State and Temple.

Paul White, Contributor: Penn State 38, Temple 21

I could definitely see this being a trap game where the Owls make it much closer than it should be. They have several former Penn State players that would love to stick it to their old school. Not to mention the fact that there is a bit of a rivalry between these schools that make the stakes even higher. I expect Penn State to win, but it could be a lot closer than last week.

Player of the game: Benjamin Brahmer, Penn State tight end

Christopher Sheppard, Contributor: Penn State 45- Temple 17

The Nittany Lions go a couple hours down the road for their first road matchup of the season against a familiar foe and a familiar face in former backup QB Jaxon Smolik. Temple is an unusual opponent with Smolik sharing snaps with the dual-threat QB Ajani Sheppard. Therefore, expect the Nittany Lions to potentially face some confusion early. Still, the blue and white should roll in this one as the defense settles in, with Tony Rojas continuing to pad his stats.

Player of the game: Tony Rojas, Penn State linebacker

Kevin McGuire, Lead Writer: Penn State 42, Temple 16

The last time Penn State walked into Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia did not go so well. But that 2015 debacle, which is still probably echoing in the nightmares of Christian Hackenberg to this day, is essentially ancient history at this point. And if last week proved anything to me, it is that Matt Campbell knows how to have his team locked in and focused no matter the opponent. I'm expecting more of the same this week against the Owls, and I think we'll see the running game having more of an impact this week. I'm not predicting any back going off for 100 rushing yards, but I do feel the combo of James Peoples and Carson Hansen will be more consistently productive than they were a week ago. But I also want to see more Koby Howard making plays with his hands too.

Player of the Game: Rocco Becht, Penn State quarterback

articles.title: Three keys to victory for Virginia ahead of their clash with Norfolk State
articles.summary: Virginia enters their Friday night contest against the Spartans as a heavy favorite
articles.body:
The Virginia Cavaliers will take the football field again after an early Week 1 bye following their Week 0 dominance over the NC State Wolfpack . On the other sideline this time out will be an in-state foe with former Virginia Tech star quarterback and college football legend Michael Vick as their head coach.

The Norfolk State Spartans come into Charlottesville with a 1-1 record, with their most recent game being their only loss of the season to the Old Dominion Monarchs , 31-10. The line Vegas opened with for this contest was 43.5 in favor of the 'Hoos and has since moved to a 45.5-point spread. Tony Elliott's squad will be expected to not only win this one, but to dominate for all four quarters.

Here is what Virginia needs to do to look back at this game and deem it a success.

Let Beau and the ground game take control early

Virginia dominated NC State on the ground by rushing for 258 yards in Week 0, with QB Beau Pribula leading the charge, accounting for 110 yards himself. Norfolk State is an FCS opponent, and Virginia has no reason to get fancy when it already knows what works against an opponent it has a huge advantage over on the ground. Establish the line of scrimmage and let Beau and the running back committee stress the Spartans out with their legs. Sprinkle in a couple of big plays through the air to satisfy the naysayers, but keep the main thing the main thing. Run the dang ball.

This feels like a key for a #2 vs. #15 seed in March Madness. The only way Norfolk State will start to gain confidence is if the Cavaliers let them. The Spartans aren't talented enough to take it themselves; they will need to be handed some gifts. They stressed ODU out last week for a half, trailing by a touchdown early in the third quarter, but that is because ODU gave them life. If Virginia stays disciplined and everyone stays committed to doing their job, this game will be a non-issue as predicted.

Virginia's defense has already opened up eyes throughout the nation when they only allowed 168 yards of total offense and eight points to NC State, and they did that without their preseason All-ACC linebacker, Kam Robinson, who will make his season debut in this week's game. This is a tremendous opportunity for Virginia to keep dominating while building depth by getting starters off the field early and giving younger guys playing time.

articles.title: Is Channing Frye's assessment of the Nets as 'garbage" fair?
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets are in the midst of a rebuild, but Channing Frye believes that the team will be garbage and currently has no identity. Is he right?
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets are in the midst of a rebuild after trading away Kevin Durant and Kyrie Irving during the 2022-23 NBA season after it became clear that something wasn't working. Brooklyn did what it could to win during the big 3 era, but since then, the Nets have been trying to build the next iteration of the team into something the fanbase can be proud of, but some around the league are not convinced.

"What do you think the Brooklyn Nets will do this season... Garbage, straight garbage. That's all right. You'll get another pick. You guys just don't have an identity," former NBA player Channing Frye said of the Nets in a YouTube Shorts video as part of his "Road Trippin" podcast. Frye was asked for his projection of Brooklyn for this upcoming season and he did not hold back.

"What is a Brooklyn Net? You guys have Michael Porter Jr. , Julius Randle , but who's your center? Who's your starting guard? You're missing a lot of pieces," Frye continued. "So, you've got got a guy or two, but you don't have a team, and you're going against the East, which is a beast this year. So, good luck." The one thing Frye was correct about was that the Eastern Conference has gotten tougher since last season.

When it comes to Frye's projection of how good the Nets will be this season, it seems that he is more on track given that most around the NBA predict that Brooklyn will finish as one of the worst teams in the Association. Depending on the source, the Nets are projected to win somewhere between 20 games and 30 games, but the more interesting part of Frye's statement was about Brooklyn's identity.

As Frye alluded to, the Nets have Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle as the headliners of the team this season, but the identify of this team has been evident since head coach Jordi Fernandez took over two seasons ago. Fernandez has made it clear to the media that any Nets player will play hard and compete the same way that he is from the sideline. If Frye watches Brooklyn play more this season, he will get a better sense of that.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes makes it clear he's over questions about leg injury
articles.summary: With Patrick Mahomes cleared to return to the Chiefs at the start of the season, Denver Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph is keeping things in persp...
articles.body:
With Patrick Mahomes cleared to return to the Chiefs at the start of the season, Denver Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph is keeping things in perspective. Joseph spoke about the return of Mahomes in media availability on Thursday

"I think Patrick is going to be Patrick. In my opinion, he wouldn't play if he couldn't be himself."

In Chiefs media availability, Mahomes bristled at consistent questions about the status of his leg heading into the prime-time Monday Night Football matchup.

"Hopefully I'm done with the questions about the leg."

Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL in his left knee during a December game against the Los Angeles Chargers , an injury severe enough that many expected him to miss multiple games to open the season. Instead, he underwent successful surgery and was cleared to return to football by July.

In comments obtained by ESPN in August, Mahomes said his goal from the outset of recovery had been to be ready for Week 1.

"It's nine months. It's the amount of time [doctors] said from the beginning, that if I did everything the right way, I would be ready to play Week One. I'm someone that, if you put [a goal] out in front of me, I want to go out and get it and maximize every single opportunity, every rep in the weight room, every hour that I can spend in the building to get my body right. This has always been the plan. From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I'll be able to go out there and be myself."

articles.title: Jake and Logan Paul are bringing a fighting reality competition to ESPN, Hulu
articles.summary: Brothers Jake and Logan Paul are expanding their reach in the fight promotion business. The brothers, former Vine and YouTube stars who have since pivoted to...
articles.body:
Brothers Jake and Logan Paul are expanding their reach in the fight promotion business. The brothers, former Vine and YouTube stars who have since pivoted to boxing and professional wrestling, respectively, plan to bring a new fighting competition show to Hulu and ESPN.

The show, currently called "Untitled Paul Brothers Fight Competition Series," is already building its cast and is set to begin production in 2027.

From the hearts and minds of Jake and Logan Paul, this series is a ruthless competition where eliminations are not settled by a vote; they are settled by a fight. Split into rival teams, coached by two rival brothers, the fighters live and train together in the wild. But the battle really begins before the fight, because fighters choose the matchups, turning every alliance, every rivalry into a strategic weapon. Jake and Logan will send the losers of each fight home until just one man and one woman are left standing to claim victory.

Jake Paul shared a message regarding the show on social media.

The repeated phrasing of "in the wild" in both Paul's message and the show's logline is interesting, as it seems to tease a Survivor-like aspect to the enterprise. Given the show was previously known under the working title of Fight Island , that sure could be the case.

While your mileage undoubtedly varies on content from the Paul brothers, they both have a history of selling fights. Jake's boxing bouts with Mike Tyson and Anthony Joshua each drew tens of millions of viewers, and his company, Most Valuable Promotions, has put together fight cards for years, while Logan fought Floyd Mayweather Jr. and has been a WWE champion.

articles.title: Russell Davis II adds to Washington's already deep pass rush rotation
articles.summary: The Washington Huskies added an "unbelievable pass rusher" back to the rotation in Russell Davis II.
articles.body:
Before Sunday's Apple Cup, it had been almost two years since Washington Huskies edge rusher Russell Davis II had last suited up for a game, but he made his presence felt immediately.

On his first snap of the season, the 6-foot-3, 225-pound pass rusher got into the Washington State backfield quickly to drop Cougars quarterback Caden Pinnick for his first sack of the season, and one of three that the Huskies tallied on the day. After an arm injury ended his 2024 season following a breakout 3-sack performance against UCLA, which earned him Big Ten Defensive Player of the Week honors, and a torn patellar tendon derailed his 2025 campaign, the sack was a big moment for Jedd Fisch and his coaching staff.

"That is Deuce Davis," Fisch said on Monday. "The guy is an unbelievable pass rusher...one out of every 12 plays he's played for us here at Washington has been a sack...the fact that we got through the game, it was his first game back after a whole year, and be productive gives us an opportunity to give him some more plays this coming week."

"It was fun to see Deuce back out there; he's got incredible power, and he's got a great speed-to-power move."

With Davis healthy, he adds to Washington's depth on the edge, where Jacob Lane, Ramzak Fruean, Logan George, and Isaiah Ward also proved in the opener that they can be productive for defensive coordinator Ryan Walters.

"I think he adds some explosiveness, some physicality, some strength on the edge," Walters said on Tuesday. "I hadn't seen him play live since I've been here, and Coach Fisch was like, 'As soon as he plays, I guarantee he's going to get a sack,' and sure enough, the first play he was in, he got a sack...It's good to see him out there; it brings us joy as a staff because of the adversity he's faced."

That sentiment resonated with a lot of his teammates, including Ward, as the pair followed Fisch from Arizona through the transfer portal in January 2024.

"It felt great," Ward added on Tuesday. "First play, first sack is something unheard of. Deuce is a great guy, and he's worked consistently, been consistent with rehab, and he's always kept a good attitude, and that was well deserved for sure."

articles.title: 3 games Miami WR Malachi Toney could cement his Heisman Trophy race
articles.summary: The Canes standout could set himself apart from the rest of the field.
articles.body:
If you haven't heard about Malachi Toney by now, you are living under a rock. The 18-year-old prodigy out of Liberty City, Florida has taken the college world by storm after his astonishing freshman season. He helped lead Miami Hurricanes to another national championship appearance.

Toney's week one performance against Stanford on Saturday will never be forgotten, literally, because he set the Miami Hurricanes ' single-game receiving record with 234 yards and a hat trick. Eddie Brown previously set the record in 1984 against Boston College with 220 receiving yards. He finished his 2025 campaign with 1,211 receiving yards, 109 receptions, and 10 touchdowns, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards at 18 years old.

Miami head coach Mario Cristobal was asked about Toney on the Pat McAfee Show and gave nothing but praise to his star-studded receiver: "He's put on 12–14 pounds of muscle man; he can accelerate and decelerate at a higher rate." Cristobal said. "He is stronger, he is faster, and then the time he puts in it's never changed, he always tries to push the envelope with that."

Cristobal's praise and the stats tell the story of the player Toney is, but three games could close the door on his competition.

Florida State struggled to stop anything SMU did in week one, but they still managed to force four turnovers against an experienced Mustangs offense. Regardless of what the stats show, rivalry games always hit a little differently. Records and past games on the schedule don't matter; it comes down to who wants to win more.

Last season when these two teams faced, Miami escaped with a 28-22 victory. The Noles also brought in Karson Hobbs, a cornerback transfer from Notre Dame ; Nehemiah Chandler, a corner from South Alabama; CJ Richard Jr, a safety from Illinois State; and Ma'khi Jones, a safety from Duke, to beef up their secondary. Despite Toney having a spectacular showing last year in Tallahassee, this year could be different.

This prediction may be a severe sleeper, but Pitt went heavy in the portal this offseason and has potential. In the secondary, Pitt returns Shawn Lee Jr., who was statistically the best in the secondary last season. He only allowed 14 catches for 71 yards and two touchdowns throughout the entire season.

In addition to Lee Jr., they added Raion Strader , a corner from Auburn and Kanye Thompson, a corner from Slippery Rock, a Division II school. According to 247Sports, Thompson earned first-team All-PSAC West honors last season and was also listed as an honorable mention All-American. At linebacker, they added a hybrid, Demarco Ward, a transfer from Memphis. He played safety for the Tigers last season but is being moved back to linebacker this season, which could help to shut down someone like Toney.

Last season, Ward had 63 tackles, three for a loss, one forced fumble, and two interceptions. Some new faces on the second and third levels of this defense should make this matchup more interesting.

Last season, Notre Dame was the 11th-ranked defense in the nation. They only allowed 17.6 points per game and 213.4 passing yards, less than Toney's receiving total against Stanford. Notre Dame's corner flew around and come down hill on the ball. In week one against Wisconsin , their only interception of the game was a pick-six, and they allowed 217 passing yards.

They held the Badgers to just 13 points in their debut, so it will be tough for Miami to just run up the score. Notre Dame showed how they could stop the run and shut down the passing lanes. Toney will have to show off his new and improved agility on the road against a pesky Notre Dame crowd.

Toney would be just the third Hurricane to win a Heisman, the first since Gino Torretta in 1992, and the first receiver in school history. He already knew this was his race to lose when he struck the Heisman pose after his first of three touchdowns against Stanford.

If he can keep the momentum going and avoid the injury bug, he could be hoisting up the trophy in December.

articles.title: Davies sinks world champion Wu at English Open
articles.summary: World champion Wu Yize is knocked out of the English Open in the third round as he loses 4-1 to Liam Davies, who faces fellow Welshman Mark Williams next.
articles.body:
World champion Wu Yize fell in the third round of the English Open as Liam Davies scored an eye-catching 4-1 victory in Brentwood.

Welsh prospect Davies, 20, opened up a 3-0 lead on his way to the first ranking event quarter-final of his career, helped by a break of 105 in the second frame, then completed his victory as China's Wu struggled to find his dynamic best form.

Tantalisingly, Davies will face compatriot Mark Williams, the three-time world champion, in the last eight on Friday evening.

Williams, still a major force on the baize at the age of 51, had breaks of 76, 103 and 63 in a late-night 4-1 victory over England's Barry Hawkins.

Mark Selby, who was runner-up at last week's British Open and won the China Open in August, had his hopes of reaching another final ended by a 4-3 defeat against fellow former world champion Kyren Wilson.

Selby led 2-0 in the all-English tussle after an early break of 112 but then lost the next three frames. He dragged himself level, but Wilson trebled in the yellow to effectively make sure of victory in the decider.

England's Judd Trump, newly deposed as world number one, edged a tense decider against Scot Anthony McGill to take a 4-3 victory.

Trump will face a quarter-final against Shaun Murphy who was taken the distance after midnight by Pang Junxu before racing through the deciding frame with a 103 break.

Ali Carter had a highest break of 75 as he completed a 4-2 win over Gong Chenzhi, Zhou Yuelong made a 141 in his 4-2 victory over Chinese compatriot Yuan Sijun, and Ding Junhui beat Joe O'Connor 4-1.
