articles.title: Caleb Downs, Cowboys’ defense will stick it to detractors in Week 1
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have some issues with their offensive line, but believers in the team have been growing. However, not everybody has bought in. But Caleb...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have some issues with their offensive line, but believers in the team have been growing . However, not everybody has bought in. But Caleb Downs and the Cowboys' defense will stick it to detractors in Week 1 and finish top-10 in 2026.

With Tyler Smith headed to IR for at least a month, the Cowboys will have to juggle their offensive line. But that won't be a problem for this juggernaut offense. The Cowboys will still score plenty of points.

The question has been all offseason: What will the defense do?

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Cowboys' defense primed to have a big year

It's not a matter of trying to be middle of the pack. The Cowboys are aiming higher. And they should. They have talented players all over the revamped unit. And new coordinator Christian Parker is the right choice to get them in the right positions to make plays.

One of the main reasons the Cowboys will be good is Downs. He's going to be a stud, beginning in Week 1. Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart will undoubtedly serve Downs an interception.

But it starts up front for the Cowboys with Quinnen Williams , according to The Athletic.

"This is a well-coached, well-built team with elite talent at multiple premium positions — most specifically: quarterback, receiver, and defensive tackle (I would count Quinnen Williams as the rare example of an interior defensive lineman in the "premium position" category)," Jourdan Rodrigue wrote.

"Defensively, the vision to significantly raise the floor is clear despite remaining questions about personnel. One of the best qualities a Super Bowl contender has is that it knows what it is, and knows what it is not (and can adjust to mask that). I don't yet know whether Dallas is a Super Bowl contender, but for once, it has this quality."

"While the offense has all the makings of a top-three unit, at least — Dak Prescott isn't thinking top three, he's thinking No. 1 — it's the other side of the ball that offers real opportunity," Zak Keefer wrote. "Jerry and Stephen Jones were so impressed with Christian Parker in the interview process that they broke out of their comfort zone and hired a first-time coordinator. For years, without exception, Dallas recycled former head coaches for that role.

"With some much-needed additions, starting with first-round pick Caleb Downs , this unit should be far more respectable this season. Paired with an elite offense, that could translate into three or four more wins."

Downs is going to make a lot of NFL general managers look silly. Here is the list of teams: Jets , Cardinals, Giants, Chiefs , Commanders (especially the Commanders), and Saints .

All of those teams passed on Downs. None of them should have. No matter the makeup of their team. And the Commanders likely made the biggest gaffe of all. They needed Downs. But they chose linebacker Sonny Styles . We've already seen in the preseason how it looks like a bad decision. It will likely end with Dan Quinn seeking employment elsewhere.

But it's the Cowboys' gain. And Downs is going to cut loose.

The Cowboys do have a few things that need to fall into place. They need DeMarvion Overshown to stay healthy. They need Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku to rush the passer effectively. Or they need Malachi Lawrence to excel as a rookie. Or perhaps Von Miller can turn back the clock and give them enough snaps on the edge.

It's a tough road ahead for teams that play the Cowboys. It's going to be tough to score 20-24 points against this defense. Good luck trying to keep the Cowboys from getting 28 or more.

Wins are the main thing. And the Cowboys will get those. It will likely start with a brutal beatdown of the Giants. Sure, the Cowboys may have some Week 1 hiccups with Parker getting his feet wet. But it shouldn't impact the bottom line.

"If the Cowboys are going to reach their goals, Parker has to be to Dallas what Steve Spagnuolo was to the 2007 New York Giants ," Jonathan Jones wrote. "It's been done before, and it will be done again. The hype around Christian Parker is real. Philadelphia knew it would lose him and still hated to see him leave.

"The Cowboys immediately involved him in free agency and draft prep. As much as you can invest in a 34-year-old stranger from a division rival to turn around your defense, Dallas has."

The defense is here. The Super Bowl hopes are real.

It's true that the defense doesn't have to stand out for the team to win games. That's because the offense believes it can score on any possession. The right pieces are in place, according to The Athletic.

"I mean it's definitely different," said Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott. "I'm optimistic going into every season kind of with that mindset. It's an NFL season. Positive vibes and good energy doesn't win you games. So, understanding that we've put ourselves in a great position. We put ourselves right where we need to be to go and give ourselves the best chance to have a great week of practice and win Week 1 up there in New York.

"Right now, the energy and everything is great, but we got to make sure we're doing everything to be accountable to each other and just continue on that trajectory. We've got to go do it. We've got to go win games."

articles.title: Mad Hatters: deGrom and Gilbert duel, Julio brings a missile launcher in 4-3 win
articles.summary: Mariners outlast deGrom, win series over Rangers thanks to big blast from Julio Rodríguez
articles.body:
So often pitchers' duels don't really stand up to the hype, but today's matchup between two former Stetson Hatters – the Mariners' Logan Gilbert and the Rangers' Jacob deGrom – delivered on all that promise and then some. The two pitchers combined for 23 strikeouts, and deGrom carried a perfect game through five innings. In true pitching duel style, it looked like the pitcher who blinked first would come out on the short end, but despite Logan Gilbert making a couple of mistakes, his offense was able to pick him up and deliver him the win. Bragging rights are fun; wins are better. (Gilbert also gets the honor of leading MLB in whiffs today: 24 to deGrom's 20, despite having one fewer strikeout than deGrom.)

This all being said, it was a slog for the Mariners early on. The best at-bat the first time through the order for the Mariners went to – surprise, surprise – Cal Raleigh , who battled deGrom for nine pitches before striking out on deGrom's fastest fastball of the day, a 99.6 mph heater (my campaign for decimal points on the ribbon board in the stadium, which read 100, continues unabated). But the Mariners did fight deGrom, getting themselves into good counts and forcing him into the zone; he finished the second inning at 37 pitches, compared to Gilbert's 24.

But it only took two pitches to offset that work in the third. Nicky Lopez was able to take 96 up and in from Gilbert and find a hole on the infield, and one batter later, with two outs, Joc Pederson jumped a first-pitch slider for a two-run homer. It wasn't a terrible pitch from Gilbert, away from Pederson but probably still too much on the plate; Gilbert had struck Pederson out on the slider in his first at-bat. The slider was particularly nasty today, with an eye-popping 75% whiff rate. He led with the pitch, throwing it 40 times, 12 times to start off an at-bat, which feels like a different sequence than he's used. Gilbert credits Cal for coming up with a good game plan, especially after he felt like he fell into some predictable patterns in his last time out against the A's.

"Like with Joc, we got him with the slider early, so he probably thought we were going to it next time," explained Gilbert. "But then also other guys, we went heavy spin, like with Duran, and then next time went three or four straight fastballs. So I think we did a good job there. They're trying to look at how we're probably scouting them, and then next time through, maybe pitch them different. I think Cal did a good job there."

But deGrom was just as tough on the other side. After striking out eight times in the first three innings, the Mariners hitters decided to try a different strategy the second time through the order. That also didn't work, as they let deGrom cruise through the fourth on nine pitches, keeping his perfect game intact.

Unfortunately, in a game that was all about which pitcher would blink first, Gilbert blinked both first and second. He made a mistake to start the fifth, hitting Evan Carter with a slider; Carter went on to steal second and then take third on an erroneous throw by Cal Raleigh, essentially making that hit by pitch a leadoff triple. Gilbert seemed to lose focus after that, walking Jake Burger after striking him out earlier, and then the Rangers were able to small-ball in a run on a bunt from Nicky Lopez that turned into a base hit when Gilbert couldn't field the weak dribbler cleanly. Nine-hole hitter Danny Jansen then bunted the runners into scoring position, but that strategy backfired as Pederson hit into a fielder's choice on a soft grounder to Naylor, erasing the runner trying to come home, and then the Rangers tried to get overly aggressive on a wild pitch from Gilbert that bounced hard off the brick backstop and directly to Cal Raleigh, where he was able to tag out Lopez trying to come home.

Finally in the sixth inning Cole Young , Perfect Boy, broke up the perfect game; in an 0-2 count he cracked a ball that glanced off deGrom's glove for an infield single and then scampered to second on a wild pitch. Young spoke yesterday after his big double about how he feels like in September he's been trying to simplify things and just focus on putting the ball in play, and he did do that here. Thank you for saving me from having to write up deGrom's perfecto, Cole, you have never been more My Favorite than you are right now.

"Obviously, I knew the perfect game was going, so I just wanted to put the ball in play," said Young postgame. "I kind of got lucky there with it hitting off his glove and then bouncing in a dead zone, so I was able to get that hit. But just trying to get on the fastball and put it in play, honestly."

The Rangers threatened again in the seventh, with Gilbert still out there; Langford led off with a walk and the Rangers made productive outs to get him to third, which brought up Lopez with two outs. With Logan pushing into the upper 90s in his pitch count, he spiked a splitter, and Langford broke for home aggressively. Cal was able to recover the ball, though, and made a nice toss to his long-term batterymate; Gilbert smacked down the tag on Langford to save a run and earn perpetual bragging rights among the starters. This is unironically one of my favorite clips of the year; I could watch it all day. (What is Logan saying there? I think it's "it's in my glove" but I can't tell.)

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video .

With deGrom finally out of the game in the seventh, the Mariners made their move. Jakob Junis started off the inning by hitting Randy, never a smart move; he then advanced to second on a wild pitch. Dominic Canzone then briefly got to hold the title of WPA leader for the day, knocking in Arozarena with a solid ground ball single and ensuring the Mariners wouldn't get shut out. Cal Raleigh followed that up with a single, extending his on-base streak to 12 games.

With Julio up to bat, Junis tried to sneak a first-pitch sinker past him. It's been a struggle at the plate lately for Julio, but this sinker arrived right in Julio's – to use a Ryon Healy-approved term – honey hole.

"I thought that ball was going to go through the back net in the bullpen," said manager Dan Wilson postgame. "There was no way the ballpark could contain it because it was just hit so hard…As we've said before, this game rewards you when you do things right, and he's been putting in the work and got a big payoff today for that."

Julio was actually out for early work yesterday – something he doesn't always do – working on his swing with his longtime organizational scout and friend (and home run derby pitcher) Franmy Pena.

"I just feel like I'm focusing on getting back to my roots," said Julio about reconnecting with his old friend. "[Franmy] was someone who signed me to the Mariners. He helped me develop back then when I was a kid, and I just feel like I needed a little refresher on things and just getting back to who I am and the things I do well."

Gabe Speier posted a clean eighth in relief of Gilbert to keep the Mariners' lead alive, setting up Andrés Muñoz for the save. Muñoz retired his first two hitters on groundouts but then walked the righty Langford, setting up a battle with Evan Carter. But Muñoz couldn't reign in his command despite being able to use his changeup against the lefty, walking Carter and bringing up the power threat Burger. In a 2-2 count, Muñoz spotted a fastball at 101.2 on the outer edge that Burger was forced to swing at, grounding it right to the steadiest hand on the Mariners' infield, Cole Young, who both stepped on second to beat out Carter and completed the throw through to first to easily beat out the slow-footed Burger, essentially getting the third and fourth outs of the inning to secure the Mariners win and the series win.

"There's just so many different layers to that play," said Young. "I wanted to make sure it didn't hit the base and get past me, so making sure of that first, and then after I caught it I'm like, okay, I've got a chance at second, let's just go there. But I knew it was going to be a bang-bang play so I started running and he's approaching second and I'm like, oh, this could be close, I don't know if I got him, so I threw it to first to make sure. I knew we got him at first, so I wasn't worried, but it was definitely a really weird play."

(Postgame when the media was thanking Young for his time, Muñoz piped up from his neighboring locker: "yes, thank you , Cole.")

The math continues to not math in the Mariners' favor, with the Astros winning today as well, but what's done is done; bragging rights might not get you to the postseason but they are a nice comfort, and for all the times his offense hasn't helped him out, it's nice for Gilbert to get that big shiny W.

articles.title: Getting to know Oklahoma ahead of matchup vs Michigan
articles.summary: Here’s what you need to know about the Oklahoma Sooners ahead of their matchup vs Michigan.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners come to Ann Arbor for the first time in history. Oklahoma is 2-0 all-time versus Michigan , but will they remain undefeated after the game on Saturday?

Here's a look at Oklahoma ahead of the showdown against Michigan.

Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables won two national championships as defensive coordinator of Clemson and is considered one of the best defensive minds in the nation. Venables is 33-20 at Oklahoma but has struggled in bowl games, going 0-4. In Oklahoma's lone playoff appearance under Venables, they lost 34-24 to Alabama in the CFP First Round last season.

Oklahoma beat UTEP 51-0 last week, holding their opponent to 2-of-13 on third-down with just 198 yards of total offense. Oklahoma's offense had 401 total yards and quarterback John Mateer threw for three passing touchdowns.

Oklahoma could have one of the best QBs in the nation

John Mateer has the ability to be electric as a runner and a thrower. Mateer's production took a dip last year, throwing for 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions after a 2024 season at Washington State with 29 touchdowns and just seven picks. Part of Mateer's 'regression' in 2026 can be attributed to him playing much of the season at less than 100% after breaking his right thumb in September and only missing one game. Mateer's grip on the ball is back to what it should be, and he'll likely revert back to his 2024 form. Even if Mateer doesn't find success, he can gash a team running. Mateer had eight rushing scores last season for 431 yards.

Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham on Oklahoma

"I can tell you right now, I've studied the personnel; they're very talented. Their defensive line is outstanding. Quarterback, we did a deep dive on him when he was at Washington State, when he went into the portal because we would have liked to have had him at Utah… he's a dual threat. A guy who can beat you both ways… They've got a game-breaking receiver… They are very talented in all three phases, and we've got our work cut out for us, big time."

Oklahoma beat Michigan 24-13 last season in Norman at Memorial Stadium. John Mateer had one passing touchdown and two rushing scores while Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood struggled, going just 9-of-22 for 142 yards. It was the first road start of Underwood's career.

Cole Sullivan looked like a promising young linebacker who could be on the path to being a great player at Michigan, but he transferred to Oklahoma this offseason and will now be taking on his former team.

"We say it's always just a nameless, faceless opponent, so that's what I'm going to do my best to treat it," Sullivan said . "Nothing's going to change in my preparation. Obviously, it's a special one, but nothing's going to change in my preparation as far as how I handle myself before the game or during the game."

Key player to watch on defense, special teams

Linebacker Kip Lewis is a tackling machine, leading the team last season with 76 tackles (10.5 for loss) with four sacks.

Receiver Isaiah Satenga returned a punt last week 88 yards for a touchdown and had 76 receiving yards and a touchdown on four receptions.

articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: World No. 1 and five-time world chess champion Magnus Carlsen has rated Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov as the favourite for his title m.
articles.body: BENGALURU: World No. 1 and five-time world chess champion Magnus Carlsen has rated Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov as the favourite for his title match against incumbent D Gukesh. The face-off starts in Geneva on Nov 24.“Chess is a highly psychological sport, so probably it won’t take a lot to — potentially — put some doubts in Sindarov’s mind and gain some confidence along the way,” Carlsen told reporters here after his team Alpine APL Pipers went down 4-12 to Ganges Grandmasters in the Global Chess League on Thursday.“But as it stands, there’s no question that Sindarov is ahead. However, if you think that a certain match is an 80:20 at the start, the likelihood is still very high that it’s going to be a one-or-two score match (number of decisive games from the 14) because chess is such a drawish game. And that means that Gukesh (has a chance). He has shown that his ceiling is on par with or better than Sindarov’s. And it’s a short match. The first few games can determine a lot. If Sindarov is ahead early on, it would probably be very, very bad news (for the Indian fans). If he is ahead early on, he automatically becomes a significant favourite. That’s how these matches work,” added the Norwegian superstar.He minced no words when he said that assessing everything on the first few games of the match is incorrect.“It’s one of the reasons why I believe it’s an extraordinarily bad way to determine the best player in the world— you play classical, which is the most egalitarian format, but you don’t play a ton of games as well,” he said.Carlsen also said that Gukesh should not be in a position where he has to “defend everything”.“The word ‘defend’ is already adding pressure (being the defending champ). It’s not a good place to begin with, going by the way Gukesh has played for the last couple of years. He should be in a position where he has everything to gain. He has shown in 2024 that when things click, he has the potential to play at an extremely high level.“While many people don’t believe he will succeed now, it’s a more interesting challenge for him to try and regain that level.”Though Carlsen had withdrawn from the World Championship cycle before the 2023 match (Ding Liren vs Ian Nepomniachtchi), he is the reigning world champion in three other FIDE events — freestyle, rapid & blitz. He is also expected to play the inaugural Total Chess World Championship tour next year, a joint venture between Norway chess organisers and FIDE that combined various time controls under one umbrella.The top-2 players from that tour will qualify for the 2028 Candidates tournament.Does this window offer fans hope to see Carlsen vs Gukesh or Sindarov matchup for the Classical World Championship? articles.title: Elon Musk feels 'chess will be fully solved one day'; what does World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen think?
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: Elon Musk picked a fight with chess earlier this week. The world's richest man declared on X that chess will one day be \"fully solved\", the.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Elon Musk picked a fight with chess earlier this week. The world's richest man declared on X that chess will one day be "fully solved", the way checkers was cracked by computers back in 2007, with his logic being that most legal moves are so obviously bad that AI could eventually map the entire game.Chess.com's response was a masterclass in brevity. "Skill issue," they wrote. Musk doubled down anyway, insisting chess "is hard for humans, but not for computers" and would eventually be "fully solved like checkers" before admitting, almost sheepishly, that he'd spent his evening "arguing with some random intern" running the chess site's account.Chess.com wasn't about to let that slide. The person on the other end, it clarified, was in fact a full-time employee. The internet, predictably, had a field day.On Thursday, the current World No. 1 and five-time world champion Magnus Carlsen was asked about the emergence of AI in chess during an interview with the Indian media on the sidelines of the ongoing Global Chess League (GCL)."I'm not a computer expert, so I don't know if it's going to be solved," Carlsen, currently playing for the defending champions APL Pipers, shrugged.He did offer one technical correction, gently. Chess isn't unsolved so much as it's already "semi-solved" in the sense that matters most to players. "We are pretty sure that it's a draw, and it's a draw in a tonne of ways. The margin is quite big", which is a rather more modest claim than Musk's vision of AI eventually calculating chess down to the last legal move."AI and computers in general have made the game a lot more accessible," he said. "You're now able to follow it, see the score, you're able to improve a lot faster."What is his motivation behind coming to India for GCL?Asked what actually motivates him to keep showing up for a franchise-based league like GCL, he made the case for team chess with the same directness. "It's a really good format," he said. "I've said that from the start that we need team formats in chess that are genuinely exciting. The black-and-white format is very good."He wasn't shy about the parts he'd still tweak, pointing to the two-second increment added after move 40 as a concession to players he clearly has little patience for."I would have preferred for there not to be the two seconds after 40 moves as well," he explained. "That has been implemented on the request of players who are incompetent and lazy at times.""The format where you have the very clear white against black, matches are staggered, which is very good. The match is always going to be decisive unless there is a six-draw. I think there are a lot of good things about it."As for India specifically, Carlsen framed his regular return trips almost like a reset button. "I also like to come to India every second year or so because I need a year off to remind myself how crowded the tournaments are," he continued with a smile before adding warmly, "But parts of it I really enjoy. There's no atmosphere or enthusiasm like it in the east."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: La financiación de la congelación de óvulos divide a las deportistas: ¿Una medida machista o una oportunidad?
articles.standfirst: La iniciativa de la RFEF ha levantado un gran debate. Pulsamos la opinión de deportistas olímpicas y paralímpicas, de varios deportes
articles.summary: La iniciativa de la RFEF ha levantado un gran debate. Pulsamos la opinión de deportistas olímpicas y paralímpicas, de varios deportes
articles.body: El debate está servido desde que El País adelantó que la Real Federación Española de Fútbol cubrirá la congelación de óvulos a las jugadoras de la selección española, a las de fútbol sala y a las árbitras de primera división el debate está servido. Esta semana la propia RFEF ha presentado el acuerdo con una clínica de fertilidad. Algunas deportistas lo interpretan como un avance, pero otras lo ven como una "medida machista" y piden que en vez de ayudar a retrasar la maternidad se ponga el foco en las medidas de conciliación para poder continuar con su carrera deportiva. Las futbolistas han acogido muy bien una medida que llega como respuesta a su propia demanda. "Estamos felices. El poder elegir cuándo y cómo queremos hacer nuestro futuro, el poder decidir, el poder informarnos... es un paso más de todos los que se están dando en la Federación", apuntó Olga Carmona en la presentación del acuerdo. "Es muy positivo (...). Lo importante es podamos no tener que elegir entre nuestra carrera profesional y nuestra vida personal", subrayó Patri Guijarro en el mismo acto. La atleta Ana Peleteiro, campeona de Europa de triple salto tras haber sido madre de su primera hija, fue la primera en alzar la voz en contra a través de sus Redes sociales. "Que no te vendan esta noticia como un progreso feminista, porque la realidad está muy lejos ello (...). Se vende esta medida como feminista cuando en realidad es profundamente machista... ¿Por qué la institución para la que trabajan estas mujeres tiene interés en que retrasen su maternidad? ¿Pretende facilitar que las mujeres sean madres o pretende que no lo sean mientras están jugando?", reflexionó en sus Redes sociales la atleta que fue bronce en Tokio 2020. "La pregunta no debería ser cómo conseguimos que una deportista retrase su maternidad sino cómo conseguimos que ser madre no penalice la carrera de una deportista", apuntó. Ona Carbonell, la nadadora más laureada en Mundiales (23 medallas) y que coordina la Comisión de Maternidad y Deporte del Comité Olímpico Español, cuestiona que se presente como una solución a la conciliación. "No puedo juzgar a la Federación Española de Fútbol porque realmente no sé el objetivo con el que han tomado esta decisión. Lo que sí puedo argumentar es que retrasar la maternidad no es conciliar. Conciliar es ayudar a que la maternidad sea factible y lo mejor posible mientras un deportista está en activo", asegura. Sobre este debate que inunda las redes sociales estos días, Paula Leitón atiende a MARCA para dar su opinión. La campeona olímpica de waterpolo ve el lado positivo a la financiación de la congelación de óvulos. “Me parece una medida fenomenal para cualquier deportista porque soy muy consciente de que la edad pico de nuestras carreras coincide con la edad en la que somos más fértiles. Estoy a favor siempre y cuando la jugadora pueda decidir qué hacer y qué priorizar", dice. "Ojalá mas federaciones se implicaran en dar información a las deportistas y que nosotras mismas podamos decidir qué hacer una vez que tengamos toda la información. Y que por supuesto respeten y apoyen nuestra decisión y los derechos asociados a ser madres igual que cualquier trabajador", añade. También responde a la llamada de MARCA Lucía Martín-Portugués, vigente campeona europea de sable y de los Juegos Mediterráneos. La madrileña ve la medida con buenos ojos. "Es importante ir avanzando. Es una medida que me parece bien. Creo que no hay que malinterpretar los avances que estamos haciendo. Es buenísima porque yo he retrasado la maternidad por mi carrera (tiene 35 años) y esta medida ayudará a quienes quieran hacerlo e incluso a las deportistas homosexuales, que les pueda ayudar a la fecundación in vitro. Es una medida buena que no hay que sacar de contexto. Lo que habría que ver son las condiciones, si te van a obligar o no a hacerlo, que eso es otra cosa", dice la sablista. La triatleta Eva Moral, bronce en los Juegos Paralímpicos de Tokio 2020, se quedó embarazada a la vuelta de aquella cita. Es muy habitual que las deportistas olímpicas y paralímpicas traten de ser madres al inicio del ciclo para que les dé tiempo a recuperarse físicamente de cara a los siguientes Juegos. Carmen, que hoy tiene cuatro años, es su mejor medalla. La madrileña reconoce a MARCA tener "sentimientos encontrados" respecto a la medida de la RFEF. "Al principio me pareció una buena medida porque se lo pagan y es algo caro, pero siempre que no sea un método de presión para que mientras estén trabajando para ellos no sean madres. Ojalá yo también hubiese tenido esa oportunidad y así no vas con esas prisas de que se te va a 'pasar el arroz'", dice viendo el lado positivo. Aunque matiza: "Pero siento que puede ser un arma de doble filo por sentir la presión de que si decides ser madre durante tu carrera deportiva se te estigmatice por no haber elegido lo otro. Lo más importante es que se tomen medidas reales de conciliación durante la época de la lactancia. Yo me sentí muy sola y poca apoyada. Perdí todo el ranking y tuve que empezar a competir cuando Carmen tenía sólo dos meses", explica a MARCA. La atleta Sara Andrés, subcampeona mundial de 100 metros, fue madre hace un año y también sabe bien lo complicado que es conciliar. "Me parece bien la medida si quieres priorizar tu carrera deportiva o porque no tengas pareja en ese momento. Es una forma de tener un recurso o un seguro. Pero si te obligan a hacerlo eso sí es descabellado", responde a nuestra llamada. La judoca Laura Martínez, diploma olímpico en París 2024, ha planteado el debate en sus propias redes esta semana. ¿Libertad para elegir o presión para esperar? "Personalmente, creo que es algo positivo siempre y cuando prevalezca la capacidad de elección de cada deportista. Yo he decidido ser madre cuando acabe mi carrera deportiva. Por eso veo esta medida como una oportunidad para que las deportistas puedan continuar con su carrera hasta que ellas mismas decidan", señala. "¿Y si una deportista decide ser madre durante su carrera? Debe contar con las ayudas necesarias para poder conciliar", añade la judoca madrileña.

articles.body:
RB Christian McCaffrey carried the ball 10 times for 68 yards versus the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1. McCaffrey was targeted eight times in the passing game, hauling in five balls for 20 yards.

Why It Matters: You never want to read too much into a single game, particularly in Week 1, but it was surprising to see how much burn Kaelon Black got. Perhaps some early big hits on CMC played a role. Perhaps San Francisco's ability to work from in front was the reason. Regardless, the rookie carried the ball 14 times in Melbourne. For comparison, last year's backup Brian Robinson averaged 5.4 carries per game and never had more than nine in a single game. McCaffrey still turned 15 touches into a respectable 88 yards, and he'll belong right back in your lineup as an RB1 in Week 2. It's a situation that bears watching, however.

articles.title: Sean McVay delivers ‘humbling’ verdict after Rams’ 49ers debacle
articles.summary: Sean McVay had no interest in blaming the Rams’ travel itinerary for their 27-7 debacle against the 49ers. “Sometimes sports can humble you, and today was on...
articles.body:
Sean McVay had no interest in blaming the Rams ' travel itinerary for their 27-7 debacle against the 49ers .

"Sometimes sports can humble you, and today was one of those days." McVay said, "I make no excuses."

The lopsided defeat immediately sparked online speculation that Los Angeles ' compressed travel schedule contributed to its lethargic performance. The Rams landed in Melbourne approximately 24 hours before kickoff, while San Francisco spent a week acclimating.

McVay would not entertain that explanation.

The numbers illustrated how thoroughly a Rams team touted as a Super Bowl favorite and "super team" was outplayed.

Los Angeles' seven points were its fewest in any game started by Matthew Stafford . The 20-point margin represented the Rams' first double-digit loss since 2024.

Myles Garrett finished without a tackle or quarterback hit for just the fourth time in his career. That disappearance was particularly jarring because Garrett generated at least one pressure in all 66 regular-season games he played from 2022-25.

The physical cost also mounted. Kam Curl departed with an ankle injury, while Davis Allen and Nate Landman also left the game.

The Rams arrived carrying an offseason's worth of championship expectations. They left with questions about their travel, conditioning and preparation — but McVay permitted only one explanation.

articles.title: 5 Chargers storylines to watch in season opener against the Cardinals
articles.summary: The Chargers will kick off their 2026 NFL regular season at home against the Cardinals. Here are five key things to watch for during the game.
articles.body:
The Chargers will kick off their 2026 NFL regular season at home against the Cardinals on Sunday, September 13, 2026, at 1:25 PM PT.

Here are the five major storylines to track during the season opener:

The most anticipated offseason storyline culminates in Mike McDaniel's regular-season debut as the Chargers ' new offensive coordinator. McDaniel is tasked with importing his explosive, motion-heavy passing concepts and marrying them with Justin Herbert 's elite arm talent. For the past two seasons under Jim Harbaugh, the Chargers operated with a more traditional, run-heavy identity. How McDaniel sequences his play calls, uses pre-snap motion to isolate defenders, and pushes the ball downfield with Herbert will dictate this offense's ceiling. Additionally, McDaniel is instilling a revamped ground game built around a wide-zone blocking scheme in hopes of maximizing sophomore running back Omarion Hampton .

A rebuilt, healthy offensive line still facing interior questions

The Chargers enter the season with a sigh of relief as their tackle tandem of Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are completely healthy after both missed significant time with injuries last year. Their presence gives Herbert premium protection against the Cardinals ' edge rushers, highlighted by Josh Sweat , but the interior of the line remains a major focal point. Kayode Awosika , who was named the starting left guard over Trey Pipkins III, will line up directly next to second-round rookie Jake Slaughter. Slaughter was thrust into the starting center role following a season-ending injury to veteran Tyler Biadasz . Compounding this new-look interior is veteran right guard Cole Strange , who arrived in free agency via a two-year, $13 million contract to reunite with McDaniel. Strange's consistency faced scrutiny from fans during the preseason. How seamlessly Awosika, Slaughter, and Strange gel as a brand-new interior unit will be absolutely vital.

After former defensive coordinator Jesse Minter left to become the Ravens ' head coach, the Chargers opted for familiarity by bringing back former safeties coach Chris O'Leary to lead the defense after serving as Western Michigan's defensive coordinator in 2025. Under Minter, Los Angeles boasted one of the NFL's best scoring defenses over the last two seasons. O'Leary's challenge in Week 1 is to prove that the unit won't suffer much of a drop-off. While the core remains intact, I am watching closely to see how effective O'Leary's more aggressive blitz approach and distinct coverage variations are against Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett .

The Chargers' defense took a hit late in training camp when veteran linebacker Denzel Perryman was placed on injured reserve. On the unofficial depth chart, Del'Shawn Phillips is the starter alongside Daiyan Henley . Phillips has historically been a special teams ace and a rotational depth piece. While Phillips is listed as the starter, I'm curious whether this will be more of a rotation, with Troy Dye and summer standout Marlowe Wax also seeing the field to determine who gets the majority of playing time.

Much of the offseason chatter revolved around how the Chargers' pass-catchers would fit into McDaniel's scheme. Out wide, all eyes are on how targets will be split between Ladd McConkey , Quentin Johnston , and Tre' Harris. At tight end, rookie standout Oronde Gadsden II was listed as the third-string tight end behind Charlie Kolar and David Njoku , suggesting the coaching staff is prioritizing blocking and traditional inline skill sets. Herbert's target distribution will offer the first real blueprint for who he establishes a rapport with.

articles.title: 'Desperate' Sabalenka books US Open title clash with Rybakina
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka stormed past Jessica Pegula in straight sets on Thursday to keep her bid for a rare US Open three-peat on track, booking a championship showd...
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka stormed past Jessica Pegula in straight sets on Thursday to keep her bid for a rare US Open three-peat on track, booking a championship showdown with Elena Rybakina.

Sabalenka was simply unstoppable in a 7-5, 6-2 victory on Arthur Ashe Stadium, where she beat Pegula en route to US Open victories in 2024 and 2025.

Rybakina battled back to beat 2023 champion Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4.

In Saturday's final the Kazakh will try to deal Sabalenka another blow after her run to the semi-finals ensured she will end the Belarusian's reign atop the world rankings.

Sabalenka, bidding to join Chris Evert and Serena Williams as the only women to win three straight US Open titles, pounded third-seeded Pegula remorselessly with her powerful groundstrokes.

"I was super desperate," said Sabalenka, who has had a slow summer since back-to-back wins at Indian Wells and Miami in March.

"I wanted it badly to go to the finals, and of course, I want to go all the way.

"The mentality was just I'm ready. I'm ready for whatever it's going to take to get the win," Sabalenka added after producing her best performance of the tournament to snuff out Pegula's dream of a first ever Grand Slam title.

Sabalenka's frustration at her inability to make any headway against Pegula's serve showed in a tense first set. But she maintained her focus and was rewarded as Pegula, feeling the pressure to stay in the set as she served down 6-5, fell behind 0-40.

The American saved one set point but couldn't salvage the next.

Sabalenka kept rolling in the second set, attacking Pegula's suspect second serve and seizing a break for a 3-1 lead when she lasered a forehand into the corner.

She sealed the victory with another break courtesy of another thunderous forehand.

"I thought her level was insanely high," Pegula said. "Honestly, I don't really know if there was much I could do today."

Rybakina, who beat Sabalenka in the Australian Open final in January to claim her second Grand Slam title, said she would need to raise her level to do the same in Flushing Meadows.

"I feel like I definitely need to step my game up, serve much better than today and stay aggressive," Rybakina said.

Gauff's bid to return to the final for the first time since she defeated Sabalenka for the 2023 title had got off to a smooth start, the American gaining the lone break of the opening set for a 4-2 lead and pocketing the set with a love game.

But Rybakina hit back with an early break on the way to a 4-1 lead in the second.

Gauff responded superbly, breaking back and holding to square the set at 4-4 to roars from the crowd.

But she was unable to make the most of her fightback and double-faulted in the 10th game to hand two set points to Rybakina, who pounced to force a third set.

Rybakina looked on the brink of victory after breaking Gauff for a 5-3 lead in the third. Gauff broke back, but Rybakina clinched it in the next game.

A deft volley from Rybakina left her with two match points and Gauff then hit a wide open smash long to hand her opponent victory.

"I feel like I was a little bit lucky on her serve," Rybakina said. "A couple of deep returns, one mistake from her, it went quickly my way...it was a real battle."

Gauff meanwhile was left reflecting on the fine margins of the defeat.

"It honestly came down to a couple of service games of mine in both sets and I didn't quite hold," Gauff said. "I think she was able to hold the line a bit better than I could tonight."

The men's semi-finals are on Friday, when eighth-seeded Ben Shelton takes on 11th seed Frances Tiafoe in an all-American clash.

Shelton took out defending champion and seven-time Grand Slam winner Carlos Alcaraz in an epic quarter-final that ended at 3:34 am on Wednesday -- the latest finish in tournament history.

"Big Ben" and "Big Foe" will duel for a chance to end American men's 23-year Grand Slam title drought.

The winner will take on either top-seeded French Open champion Alexander Zverev or unseeded Russian Karen Khachanov.

Darian Mensah showed off dominance in convincing fashion as he and the No. 7 Miami Hurricanes cruised to a 77-7 win over the FAMU Rattlers on Thursday night.

Mensah has started the fourth year of his collegiate career, his first with the Hurricanes. Following stints at Tulane and Duke, he joined Miami with the goal of competing for a national championship. The Hurricanes reached that stage last season before losing to Indiana, making the objective a lofty one for Mensah.

That doesn't mean he will back down form the challenge. Quite the opposite following his first two games for Miami.

articles.title: Patriots Rejected Trade Interest in $8.4 Million Ex-Buffalo Bills WR Before A.J. Brown Injury: Report
articles.summary: The New England Patriots had another opportunity to refashion their congested wide receiver room before the season.This time, they declined, luckily doing so...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots had another opportunity to refashion their congested wide receiver room before the season.

This time, they declined, luckily doing so without knowing A.J. Brown 's injury was coming in the future.

Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer revealed on 98.5 The Sports Hub that an NFL team showed interest in Mack Hollins several weeks before the Patriots ultimately traded Kayshon Boutte .

"Four or five weeks ago," an unnamed team contacted Breer about whether New England would consider moving Hollins, Breer explained on Sept. 10.

Breer brought up Boutte as a possible alternative. The interested team indicated it would rather have Hollins, according to Breer, who then checked on Hollins' availability with the Patriots.

The revelation adds more context to the Patriots' late-summer decision-making at receiver. They eventually sent Boutte to the Houston Texans , but Hollins remained in Foxborough — and one game into the season, that choice already is of import.

Patriots Chose Hollins Over Another Potential Trade

Boutte's departure became official Aug. 24, when New England dealt him to Houston for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick.

The Patriots had created a numbers crunch by adding A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs during the offseason. Boutte, meanwhile, had been the subject of trade speculation well before training camp.

Executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf later pointed to the variety within the receiver room when explaining the move.

"We feel really good about our receiver group," Wolf said, via NFL.com , adding that New England valued receivers who could fill different positions, block and contribute on special teams.

Head coach Mike Vrabel offered an even clearer explanation after the trade.

He said Boutte likely would have been inactive without injuries elsewhere on the roster because he didn't contribute on special teams.

New England ended up keeping Hollins, Brown, Doubs, DeMario Douglas , Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III on its initial 53-man roster. The Patriots' roster analysis described the position as loaded after the offseason overhaul.

Breer's latest information suggests Hollins was viewed differently around the league, too. At least one club preferred the veteran to Boutte when presented with both possibilities.

Hollins' Value Becomes Clear After A.J. Brown Injury

Keeping Hollins could become particularly important after one week.

The 32-year-old led New England with four catches for 51 yards during its 13-10 season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks .

Hollins is coming off a productive first season in New England in which he caught 46 passes for 550 yards and two touchdowns in 15 games. He started 13 contests and became a steady piece of the offense during the Patriots' run to Super Bowl LX.

Brown exited the opener with an ankle injury, and NFL Network reported he is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain. Vrabel said Thursday that Brown will undergo additional testing and acknowledged his availability going forward is uncertain, via the Patriots , but the most recent update notes a high ankle sprain with an 4-week timeline "at least."

That leaves Hollins as an increasingly vital target for Drake Maye as New England sorts through Brown's status.

So, the Patriots' refusal now looks consequential, which gives more context to why Boutte, instead of Hollins, became the receiver they moved.

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers Wide Receiver Suddenly Exits Rams Game With Unfortunate Injury
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers have officially begun their NFL season on Thursday night with a Week 1 divisional showdown against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne,...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have officially begun their NFL season on Thursday night with a Week 1 divisional showdown against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia.

While San Francisco started the scoring with a field goal, the Rams quickly responded with a Kyren Williams rushing touchdown to take the lead.

However, the early story for the 49ers centered around rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling, who exited the game with an apparent ankle injury.

After limping off the field and entering the medical tent, the 49ers posted on social media that Stribling, who has had a tremendous offseason, is questionable to return.

Via the 49ers: " #49ers @SutterHealth Injury Update: De'Zhaun Stribling is questionable to return (ankle)."

San Francisco selected Stribling out of Ole Miss with the No. 33 overall pick in the second round, and he's firmly emerged as one of the wide receivers expected to see serious playing time this season.

UPDATE: Stribling Returns to Game and Gets Re-Injured

Roughly 20 minutes after exiting the contest, Stribling stepped back onto the field. Yet, on his very first route across the middle, he fell to the ground and once again grabbed his foot/ankle area.

He had to be helped off the field this time by trainers in obvious pain.

This story will be updated as reports emerge…
